title.en: Volume 254 Biographies 142: Qiao Yunsheng, Cao Yubian, Sun Juxiang, Cao Guang, Chen Yuting, Zheng Sanjun, Li Rixuan, Zhang Wei
title.raw: 卷二百五十四 列傳第一百四十二 喬允升 曹于汴 孫居相 曹珖 陳于庭 鄭三俊 李日宣 張瑋 Volume 254 Biographies 142: Qiao Yunsheng, Cao Yubian, Sun Juxiang, Cao Guang, Chen Yuting, Zheng Sanjun, Li Rixuan, Zhang Wei

sentences.zh: 喬允升

translations.literal: Qiao Yunsheng
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yunsheng

sentences.zh: （易應昌等）〉

translations.literal: (Yi Yingchang et al. appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Yi Yingchang et al. appended)〉

sentences.zh: 曹於汴孫居相

translations.literal: Cao Yubian Sun Juxiang
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yubian and Sun Juxiang

sentences.zh: （弟鼎相）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brother Dingsiang appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Younger brother Dingsiang appended)〉

sentences.zh: 曹光陳於廷鄭三俊李日宣張瑋

translations.literal: Cao Guang Chen Yuting Zheng Sanjun Li Rixuan Zhang Wei
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guang, Chen Yuting, Zheng Sanjun, Li Rixuan, and Zhang Wei

sentences.zh: （金光辰）〉

translations.literal: (Jin Guangchen appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Jin Guangchen appended)〉

sentences.zh: 喬允升，字吉甫，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Qiao Yunsheng, style name Jifu, was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yunsheng, whose style was Jifu, came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除太谷知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Taigu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Taigu county.

sentences.zh: 以治行高等征授御史。

translations.literal: Because his record of governance ranked high, he was summoned and made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of an outstanding administrative record, he was called to the capital and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 歷按宣、大、山西、畿輔，並著風采。

translations.literal: In succession he toured and inspected Xuan, Da, Shanxi, and the capital region, everywhere winning renown for his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as touring censor for Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and the metropolitan districts, and everywhere earned a reputation for forceful integrity.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，大計京官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year came the grand evaluation of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year the court conducted its grand evaluation of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 允升協理河南道，力鋤匪類。

translations.literal: Yunsheng assisted in managing the Henan circuit and strove to root out villainous types.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng helped oversee the Henan circuit and worked hard to purge corrupt and unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 而主事秦聚奎、給事中朱一桂鹹為被察者訟冤。

translations.literal: But the section chief Qin Jukui and the supervising secretary Zhu Yigui all pleaded the innocence of those marked for dismissal in the inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Section chief Qin Jukui and supervising secretary Zhu Yigui, however, all petitioned on behalf of officials slated for removal, claiming they had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 察疏猶未下，允升慮帝意動搖，三疏別白其故，且劾吏部侍郎蕭雲舉佐察行私，事乃獲竣，雲舉亦引去。

translations.literal: The inspection memorial had not yet been issued; Yunsheng feared the emperor's resolve might waver, submitted three memorials clarifying the reasons separately, and also impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Yunju for abetting the inspection in private dealings; only then was the matter brought to completion, and Yunju also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before the inspection report could be promulgated, Yunsheng feared the emperor might waver. He submitted three memorials setting out the facts in detail and also impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Yunju for using the inspection to pursue private ends. The evaluation was finally concluded, and Yunju resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 尋遷順天府丞，進府尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture and advanced to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture and then to prefect.

sentences.zh: 齊、楚、浙三黨用事，移疾歸。

translations.literal: The three factions of Qi, Chu, and Zhe held power; he resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions came to dominate the court, he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起歷刑部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was recalled and served in succession as left and right vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianqi reign began, he was recalled and served successively as left and right vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 三年，進尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢逐吏部尚書趙南星，廷推允升代。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian drove out Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing; the court recommended Yunsheng to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian ousted Zhao Nanxing from the Ministry of Personnel, and the court nominated Yunsheng to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 忠賢以允升為南星黨，並逐主議者，允升復移疾歸。

translations.literal: Zhongxian, taking Yunsheng as a member of Nanxing's faction, also drove out those who had led the recommendation; Yunsheng again resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian treated Yunsheng as one of Nanxing's party and purged those who had backed his nomination as well. Yunsheng once more resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 既而給事中薛國觀劾允升主謀邪黨，詔落職閑住。

translations.literal: Thereafter the supervising secretary Xue Guoguan impeached Yunsheng as chief plotter of an evil faction; an edict stripped him of office and ordered him to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward supervising secretary Xue Guoguan accused Yunsheng of masterminding a corrupt faction, and an edict removed him from office and confined him to private life.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，召拜故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was summoned and reappointed to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 時訟獄益繁，帝一切用重典。

translations.literal: At the time lawsuits and criminal cases grew ever more numerous, and the emperor applied severe punishments across the board.
translations.idiomatic: Litigation was mounting, and the emperor resorted to harsh penalties in every case.

sentences.zh: 允升執法不撓，多所平反。

translations.literal: Yunsheng enforced the law without yielding and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng held firm to the law and reversed numerous unjust verdicts.

sentences.zh: 先是，錢謙益典試浙江。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qian Qianyi had presided over the provincial examination in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qian Qianyi had served as chief examiner for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 有奸人金保元、徐時敏偽作關節，授舉子錢千秋，千秋故有文，獲薦，覺保元、時敏詐，與之哄。

translations.literal: Wicked men Jin Baoyuan and Xu Shimin forged examination leak materials and gave them to the candidate Qian Qianqiu; Qianqiu was already gifted in letters and obtained recommendation, but on discovering Baoyuan and Shimin's fraud he quarreled with them.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers Jin Baoyuan and Xu Shimin forged leaked examination passages and passed them to the candidate Qian Qianqiu. Qianqiu was already a skilled writer and won recommendation, but when he realized the fraud he quarreled with the two men.

sentences.zh: 事傳京師，為部、科磨勘者所發。

translations.literal: The affair reached the capital and was exposed by reviewers in the ministries and supervising secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the capital, and investigators in the ministries and censorate uncovered the case.

sentences.zh: 謙益大駭，詰知二奸所為，疏劾之，並千秋俱下吏。

translations.literal: Qianyi was greatly alarmed; on interrogation he learned what the two villains had done, memorialized to impeach them, and both Qianqiu and they were handed to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was deeply shaken. Once he learned what the two men had done, he memorialized to impeach them, and Qianqiu was sent to the courts along with them.

sentences.zh: 罪當戍，二奸瘐死，千秋更赦釋還。

translations.literal: The sentence called for banishment; the two villains died in prison of illness, and Qianqiu was later pardoned and released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was exile, but the two schemers died in custody. Qianqiu was later pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 事已七年矣，溫體仁以枚卜不與，疑謙益主之，復發其事。

translations.literal: The matter was already seven years past when Wen Tiren, not having been chosen in the ministerial sortition, suspected Qianyi had engineered it and revived the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years had passed when Wen Tiren, passed over in the ministerial sortition, suspected Qianyi had blocked him and reopened the case.

sentences.zh: 詔逮千秋再訊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qianqiu seized for re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qianqiu arrested and tried again.

sentences.zh: 帝深疑廷臣結黨，蓄怒以待，而體仁又密伺於旁，廷臣相顧惕息。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply suspected that court ministers were forming factions; he nursed anger and waited, while Tiren also watched secretly from the side; the ministers looked at one another in fear and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was convinced the court was faction-ridden and nursed his wrath, while Tiren watched from the shadows. Ministers glanced at one another in dread.

sentences.zh: 允升乃會都御史曹於汴、大理卿康新民等讞鞫者再，千秋受拷無異詞，允升等具以聞。

translations.literal: Yunsheng then joined Censor-in-Chief Cao Yubian, Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Kang Xinmin, and others in trying the case a second time; under torture Qianqiu made no change in his testimony, and Yunsheng and the rest reported fully to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng joined Censor-in-Chief Cao Yubian, Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Kang Xinmin, and others in a second trial. Under torture Qianqiu did not alter his confession, and they reported the result to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，命覆勘。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and ordered a further review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and ordered the case reviewed again.

sentences.zh: 體仁慮謙益事白，己且獲譴，再疏劾法官六欺，且言獄詞盡出謙益手。

translations.literal: Tiren, fearing that if Qianyi's case were cleared he himself would be punished, again memorialized impeaching the judges for six deceptions, and said the prison depositions had all come from Qianyi's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that if Qianyi were cleared he would be punished himself, Tiren memorialized again, accusing the judges of six kinds of deceit and claiming the trial record had been written entirely by Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 允升憤，求去。

translations.literal: Yunsheng, in anger, requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng, furious, asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝雖慰留，卒如體仁言，奪謙益官閑住。

translations.literal: Although the emperor comforted him and kept him in office, in the end he followed Tiren's words, stripped Qianyi of office, and ordered him to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urged him to stay, but in the end heeded Tiren: Qianyi was stripped of office and sent into retirement.

sentences.zh: 千秋荷校死。

translations.literal: Qianqiu died bearing the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu died in the cangue.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，我大清兵薄都城，獄囚劉仲金等百七十人破械出，欲逾城，被獲。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year, our Great Qing forces pressed close to the capital; one hundred seventy prisoners including Liu Zhongjin broke their fetters and came out, intending to scale the walls, and were seized.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the second year of the reign, Qing forces approached the capital. One hundred seventy prisoners led by Liu Zhongjin broke their shackles and tried to escape over the wall but were captured.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，下允升及左侍郎胡世賞、提牢主事敖繼榮獄，欲置之死。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with rage and sent Yunsheng, Left Vice Minister Hu Shishang, and the prison registrar Aoji Rong to jail, intending to put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and imprisoned Yunsheng, Vice Minister Hu Shishang, and prison registrar Aoji Rong, intending to execute them.

sentences.zh: 中書沈自植乘間摭劾允升他罪，章並下按問。

translations.literal: The Secretariat drafter Shen Zizhi seized the opportunity to gather charges and impeach Yunsheng on other crimes; the memorial was also sent down for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Shen Zizhi seized the moment to compile further charges against Yunsheng, and that memorial too was sent for investigation.

sentences.zh: 副都御史掌院事易應昌以允升等無死罪，執奏再三，帝益怒，並下應昌獄，鐫僉都御史高弘圖、大理寺卿金世俊級，奪少卿周邦基以下俸，令再讞。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief and acting head of the court Yi Yingchang held that Yunsheng and the others had no capital crime; he memorialized repeatedly, but the emperor grew angrier still, sent Yingchang to prison as well, reduced Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Hongtu and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Jin Shijun in rank, stripped the salaries of Junior Minister Zhou Bangji and those below, and ordered a new judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yi Yingchang, acting head of the Censorate, insisted that Yunsheng and the others deserved no death sentence and memorialized again and again. The emperor only grew angrier, imprisoned Yingchang as well, demoted Gao Hongtu and Jin Shijun, docked the salaries of Zhou Bangji and other junior officials, and ordered the case retried.

sentences.zh: 弘圖等乃坐允升絞，而微言其年老可念。

translations.literal: Hongtu and the rest then sentenced Yunsheng to strangulation, while hinting that his advanced age might be taken into account.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtu and the others then imposed strangulation on Yunsheng, while quietly noting that his age might merit mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝謂允升法當死，特高年篤疾減死，與繼榮俱戍邊，世賞贖杖為民。

translations.literal: The emperor said Yunsheng by law deserved death but, in special consideration of his great age and grave illness, reduced the sentence; he and Jirong were both banished to the frontier, while Shishang ransomed flogging and became a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared that Yunsheng deserved death by law but, given his age and illness, commuted the sentence. He and Jirong were banished to the frontier; Shishang paid a fine in lieu of flogging and was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 尚書胡應臺等上應昌罪，帝以為輕。

translations.literal: Minister Hu Yingtai and others reported Yingchang's crimes; the emperor thought the penalty too light.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Hu Yingtai and others submitted the charges against Yingchang, but the emperor found the proposed punishment too lenient.

sentences.zh: 杖郎中徐元嘏於廷，鐫應臺秩視事，應昌論死。

translations.literal: The director Xu Yuangeng was beaten at court; Yingtai was reduced in rank but continued in office; Yingchang was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xu Yuangeng was flogged in court. Yingtai was demoted but kept at his post. Yingchang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，久旱求言，多請緩刑，乃免應昌及工部尚書張鳳翔、御史李長春、給事中杜齊芳、都督李如楨死，遣戍邊衛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, after prolonged drought the court sought advice; many asked that punishments be eased, and so Yingchang and Minister of Works Zhang Fengxiang, Censor Li Changchun, Supervising Secretary Du Qifang, and Commander Li Ruzhen were spared death and sent to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, after a long drought the court called for memorials. Many urged clemency, and Yingchang was spared along with Zhang Fengxiang, Li Changchun, Du Qifang, and Li Ruzhen—all commuted to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 允升赴戍所，未幾死。

translations.literal: Yunsheng went to his place of banishment and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng set out for exile and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 允升端方廉直，揚歷中外，具有聲績，以詿誤獲重譴，天下惜之。

translations.literal: Yunsheng was upright, incorruptible, and straightforward; he had served with distinction inside and outside the capital and possessed a record of achievement, yet through entanglement in error received severe punishment, and all under Heaven regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and incorruptible, Yunsheng had served with distinction at court and in the provinces, yet a mishap brought him severe punishment, and the empire mourned his fall.

sentences.zh: 易應昌，字瑞芝，臨川人。

translations.literal: Yi Yingchang, style name Ruizhi, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yingchang, whose style was Ruizhi, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，由御史累遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xizong he rose in succession from censor to junior minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xizong emperor he rose from censor to junior minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 逆黨劾為東林，削籍。

translations.literal: The faction in power impeached him as a member of the Donglin faction and struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The ruling faction denounced him as a Donglin partisan and struck his name from the register.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起左僉都御史，進左副都御史，與曹於汴持史褷、高捷起官事，為時所重，至是獲罪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was raised to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief; with Cao Yubian he resisted the reinstatement of Shi Shi and Gao Jie, and was highly regarded in his time—until he incurred guilt on this occasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen he was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and then Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. With Cao Yubian he opposed reinstating Shi Shi and Gao Jie, winning wide respect—until this case brought him down.

sentences.zh: 福王時，召復故官，遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was summoned back to his former post and transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was recalled to his former post and promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 國變後卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic upheaval he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after the fall of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝在位十七年，刑部易尚書十七人。

translations.literal: During the emperor's seventeen years on the throne, the Ministry of Justice changed ministers seventeen times.
translations.idiomatic: In the emperor's seventeen years on the throne, the Ministry of Justice had seventeen ministers.

sentences.zh: 薛貞以奄黨抵死，蘇茂相半歲而罷，王在晉，未任改兵部去，允升遣戍，韓繼思坐議獄除名，胡應臺獨得善去，馮英被劾遣戍，鄭三俊坐議獄逮系，劉之鳳坐議獄論絞，瘐死獄中，甄淑坐納賄下詔獄，改系刑部，瘐死，李覺斯坐議獄削籍去，劉澤深卒於位，鄭三俊再為尚書，改吏部，範景文未任，改工部，徐石麒坐議獄落職閑住，胡應臺再召不赴，繼其後者張忻，賊陷京師，與子庶吉士端並降。

translations.literal: Xue Zhen died for his ties to the eunuch faction; Su Maoxiang was dismissed after half a year; Wang Zaijin, before taking office, was transferred to the Ministry of War and left; Yunsheng was banished; Han Jisi was struck from the rolls for involvement in a disputed case; Hu Yingtai alone departed with honor; Feng Ying was impeached and banished; Zheng Sanjun was arrested for involvement in a disputed case; Liu Zhifeng was sentenced to strangulation in a disputed case and died of illness in prison; Zhen Shu was imprisoned in the imperial prison for taking bribes, then transferred to the Ministry of Justice, and died of illness; Li Juesi was struck from the rolls and left for involvement in a disputed case; Liu Zeshen died in office; Zheng Sanjun again became minister, then was transferred to Personnel; Fan Jingwen, before taking office, was transferred to Works; Xu Shiqi was stripped of office and ordered to live in retirement for involvement in a disputed case; Hu Yingtai, when summoned again, did not come; his successor Zhang Xin, when bandits took the capital, surrendered together with his son Duan, a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhen was executed as an eunuch partisan; Su Maoxiang lasted half a year; Wang Zaijin was shifted to the Ministry of War before he could take office; Yunsheng was exiled; Han Jisi was struck from the rolls over a political trial; Hu Yingtai alone left with his reputation intact; Feng Ying was impeached and banished; Zheng Sanjun was jailed in a political case; Liu Zhifeng was condemned to strangulation in another such case and died in prison; Zhen Shu entered the imperial prison for bribery, was moved to the Ministry of Justice, and died there; Li Juesi was struck from the rolls in yet another political trial; Liu Zeshen died in office; Zheng Sanjun served again, then moved to Personnel; Fan Jingwen never took office in Justice, being transferred to Works; Xu Shiqi was removed in a political case; Hu Yingtai declined a second summons; his successor Zhang Xin surrendered with his son Duan, a Hanlin bachelor, when the rebels took the capital.

sentences.zh: 曹於汴，字自梁，安邑人。

translations.literal: Cao Yubian, style name Ziliang, was a native of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yubian, whose style was Ziliang, came from Anyi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十九年舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Wanli he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Wanli he topped the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年成進士，授淮安推官。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed investigating censor of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed investigating censor in Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 以治行高第，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Because his record of governance ranked high, he was made a supervising secretary in the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of an outstanding administrative record, he was made a supervising secretary in the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 疏劾兩京兵部尚書田樂、邢玠及雲南巡撫陳用賓，樂、玠遂引去。

translations.literal: He memorialized to impeach the Ministers of War of the two capitals Tian Le and Xing Jie, and the Yunnan grand coordinator Chen Yongbin; Le and Jie thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against the Ministers of War at both capitals, Tian Le and Xing Jie, and against Yunnan grand coordinator Chen Yongbin. Tian and Xing resigned.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎趙邦清被誣，於汴疏雪之。

translations.literal: The bureau director Zhao Bangqing had been slandered; Yubian memorialized to clear him.
translations.idiomatic: When bureau director Zhao Bangqing was falsely accused, Yubian memorialized to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 謁告歸，僦屋以居，不蔽風日。

translations.literal: On leave he returned home and rented a house to live in that could not keep out wind and sun.
translations.idiomatic: On leave he went home and rented a dwelling so poor it scarcely kept out wind and weather.

sentences.zh: 起歷刑科左、右給事中。

translations.literal: On recall he served in succession as left and right supervising secretary in the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he served successively as left and right supervising secretary in the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 朝房災，請急補曠官，修廢政。

translations.literal: When the court chambers burned, he asked that vacant offices be filled urgently and neglected policies be restored.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the court chambers, he urged prompt filling of vacant posts and revival of neglected reforms.

sentences.zh: 遼左有警，朝議增兵，於汴言：「國家三歲遣使者閱邊，盛獎邊臣功伐，蟒衣金幣之賜，官秩之增，未嘗或靳。

translations.literal: When there was alarm on the Liaodong frontier, the court debated increasing troops; Yubian said: "Every three years the state sends envoys to inspect the borders, lavishly praising frontier officials' achievements, with gifts of python robes and gold coins and promotions in rank never stinted.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble flared on the Liaodong frontier, the court debated reinforcing the armies. Yubian said: "Every three years the court sends inspectors to the borders, lavishing praise on frontier commanders, granting python robes and gold, and promoting their ranks without stint.

sentences.zh: 今廢防至此，宜重加按問。

translations.literal: Now that defenses have fallen to this pass, they should be sternly investigated again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet defenses have collapsed to this point. Those responsible should be rigorously investigated.

sentences.zh: 邊道超擢，當於秩滿時閱實其績，毋徒循資俸，坐取建牙開府。

translations.literal: For extraordinary promotion on the frontier, their achievements should be verified when their term of rank is complete, and they should not merely follow seniority in salary to sit and obtain the establishment of military banners and opening of a grand headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary promotions on the frontier should follow a full review of actual achievement at term's end, not mere seniority that lets men raise banners and open grand headquarters without merit.

sentences.zh: 」進吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡嘉棟發中官陳永壽兄弟奸，永壽反訐嘉棟。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Hu Jiadong exposed the crimes of the eunuch Chen Yongshou and his brothers; Yongshou in turn accused Jiadong.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Hu Jiadong exposed the eunuch Chen Yongshou and his brothers; Yongshou counter-attacked.

sentences.zh: 於汴極論永壽罪。

translations.literal: Yubian argued Yongshou's crimes to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Yubian pressed the case against Yongshou with full force.

sentences.zh: 故事，章疏入會極門，中官直達之御前，至是必啟視然後進禦。

translations.literal: By precedent, when memorials entered the Gate of Ultimate Polarity, eunuchs carried them straight to the emperor's presence; from this time they had to be opened and read before being forwarded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent memorials entering the Gate of Ultimate Polarity were carried straight to the emperor by eunuchs. Now they had to be opened and read before reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 於汴謂乖祖制，泄事機，力請禁之。

translations.literal: Yubian said this violated ancestral institutions and leaked state secrets, and he strongly asked that it be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Yubian argued this violated ancestral practice and leaked state secrets, and he pressed hard for a ban.

sentences.zh: 三十八年典外察，去留悉當。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he presided over the outer inspection; dismissals and retentions were all appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he ran the outer inspection, and every dismissal and retention was judged fairly.

sentences.zh: 明年，典京察，屏湯賓尹、劉國縉等，而以年例出王紹徽、喬慶甲於外。

translations.literal: The next year he presided over the capital inspection, excluding Tang Binyin, Liu Guojin, and others, while by the annual rule sending Wang Shaohui and Qiao Qingjia outside.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he ran the capital inspection, removing Tang Binyin, Liu Guojin, and others, while Wang Shaohui and Qiao Qingjia were sent out under the regular rotation rule.

sentences.zh: 其黨群起力攻，於汴持之堅，卒不能奪。

translations.literal: Their faction rose together to attack with force; Yubian held firm and in the end they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Their faction attacked in force, but Yubian held firm and they could not overturn his decisions.

sentences.zh: 以久次擢太常少卿，疏寢不下，請告又不報，候命歲餘，移疾歸。

translations.literal: Because of long seniority he was promoted to Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his memorials lay dormant without response, his requests for leave went unanswered, he waited on orders for more than a year, then resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Long service won him promotion to Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, but his memorials went unanswered and his requests for leave were ignored. After more than a year waiting on orders, he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，始以太常少卿召。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was first summoned as Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Yubian was first recalled as Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 至則改大理少卿，遷左僉都御史，佐趙南星京察。

translations.literal: On arrival he was changed to Junior Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and assisted Zhao Nanxing in the capital inspection.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was shifted to the Court of Judicial Review, then made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and assisted Zhao Nanxing in the capital inspection.

sentences.zh: 事竣，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded, he was advanced to Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspection ended, he was promoted to Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年秋，吏部缺右侍郎，廷推馮從吾，以於汴副，中旨特用於汴。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Tianqi the Ministry of Personnel lacked a right vice minister; the court recommended Feng Congwu with Yubian as deputy, but an imperial rescript specially appointed Yubian.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tianqi year three the Ministry of Personnel needed a right vice minister. The court nominated Feng Congwu with Yubian as alternate, but an imperial rescript appointed Yubian instead.

sentences.zh: 於汴以從吾名位先己，義不可越，四辭不得，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Yubian, holding that Congwu's fame and rank preceded his own and that propriety forbade passing over him, declined four times without success, then resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yubian held that Feng Congwu outranked him and that propriety forbade stepping ahead of him. He declined four times, was overruled, and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年，起南京右都御史，辭不拜。

translations.literal: The next year he was raised to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing but declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was offered the post of Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing but refused it.

sentences.zh: 時紹徽、應甲附魏忠賢得誌，必欲害於汴，屬其黨石三畏以東林領袖劾之，遂削奪。

translations.literal: At the time Shaohui and Yingjia, having attached themselves to Wei Zhongxian and gained their will, were determined to harm Yubian; they had their partisan Shi Sanwei impeach him as leader of the Donglin faction, and he was stripped and penalized.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohui and Yingjia, having attached themselves to Wei Zhongxian, were determined to destroy Yubian. They had their partisan Shi Sanwei impeach him as a Donglin leader, and he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，召拜左都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 振舉憲規，約敕僚吏，臺中肅然。

translations.literal: He raised and enforced disciplinary regulations, admonished his subordinate officials, and the Censorate became austere and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He revived censorial discipline, restrained his staff, and the Censorate became a model of order.

sentences.zh: 明年京察，力汰匪類，忠賢余黨幾盡，仕路為清。

translations.literal: The next year in the capital inspection he strove to purge villainous types; Zhongxian's remaining partisans were nearly all gone, and the path of office became clean.
translations.idiomatic: The next year's capital inspection purged the corrupt almost to a man, nearly wiping out Zhongxian's remaining allies and clearing the road to office.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁訐錢謙益，下錢千秋法司，訊不得實，體仁以於汴謙益座主也，並訐之。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren accused Qian Qianyi; Qian Qianqiu was sent to the judicial authorities, and the interrogation found no substance; Tiren, because Yubian was Qianyi's examination patron, accused him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren attacked Qian Qianyi and sent Qian Qianqiu to the courts, but the trial found no proof. Tiren then attacked Yubian as well, since Yubian had been Qianyi's examination patron.

sentences.zh: 於汴亦發體仁欺罔狀。

translations.literal: Yubian also exposed Tiren's deceitful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yubian in turn exposed Tiren's deceptions.

sentences.zh: 帝終信體仁，謙益竟獲罪。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end trusted Tiren, and Qianyi ultimately incurred punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately sided with Tiren, and Qianyi was punished.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔定逆案。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had fixed the case of traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had established the roster of traitors from the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 於汴與大學士韓爌、李標、錢龍錫，刑部尚書喬允升平心參決，不為已甚，小人猶惡之。

translations.literal: Yubian joined Grand Secretaries Han Kuang, Li Biao, and Qian Longxi, and Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng in judging with even mind and not going too far, yet petty men still hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yubian joined Grand Secretaries Han Kuang, Li Biao, and Qian Longxi and Minister Qiao Yunsheng in judging the case even-handedly and without excess, yet petty men still hated them for it.

sentences.zh: 故御史高捷、史褷素憸邪，為清議所擯，吏部尚書王永光力薦之。

translations.literal: The former censors Gao Jie and Shi Shi had always been treacherous and depraved and were rejected by pure criticism; Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang strongly recommended them.
translations.idiomatic: Former censors Gao Jie and Shi Shi were notoriously corrupt and had been ostracized by upright opinion, yet Minister Wang Yongguang strongly recommended them for reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史起官，必都察院咨取，於汴惡其人，久弗咨。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a censor was raised to office the Censorate had to be consulted for selection; Yubian detested these men and for long did not consult.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent reinstating a censor required consultation with the Censorate. Yubian despised the men and for a long time refused to consult.

sentences.zh: 永光憤，再疏力爭。

translations.literal: Yongguang, in anger, memorialized again and strove with force.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang, furious, memorialized again and fought the decision fiercely.

sentences.zh: 已得請，於汴猶以故事持之，兩人遂投牒自乞，於汴益惡之，卒持不予。

translations.literal: Though permission had been granted, Yubian still held to precedent; the two men thereupon submitted petitions asking for themselves, Yubian hated them all the more, and in the end held firm and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Even after approval was granted, Yubian still insisted on precedent. The two men petitioned on their own behalf, which only deepened Yubian's hostility, and he ultimately refused to consult.

sentences.zh: 兩人竟以部疏起官，遂日夜謀傾於汴。

translations.literal: The two men in the end were raised to office through a ministry memorial, and then day and night plotted to overthrow Yubian.
translations.idiomatic: They were reinstated anyway through a Ministry memorial and then plotted day and night to bring Yubian down.

sentences.zh: 中書原抱奇者，賈人子也，嘗誣劾大學士爌。

translations.literal: The Secretariat drafter Yuan Baoqi was a merchant's son and had once falsely impeached Grand Secretary Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Yuan Baoqi was a merchant's son who had once falsely impeached Grand Secretary Han Kuang.

sentences.zh: 至是再劾爌及於汴並及尚書孫居相、侍郎程啟南、府丞魏光緒，目為「西黨」，請皆放黜，以五人籍山西也。

translations.literal: At this time he again impeached Kuang and Yubian, and also Minister Sun Juxiang, Vice Minister Cheng Qinan, and Prefecture Vice Magistrate Wei Guangxu, labeling them the "Western Faction" and asking that all be dismissed, because the five men's registers were in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Now he impeached Han Kuang and Yubian again, along with Minister Sun Juxiang, Vice Minister Cheng Qinan, and Vice Magistrate Wei Guangxu, branding them the "Western Faction" and demanding their dismissal—all five being natives of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 帝絀抱奇言不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Baoqi's words and did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Baoqi and ignored his charges.

sentences.zh: 而工部主事陸澄源復劾於汴朋奸六罪。

translations.literal: But the Works section chief Lu Chengyuan again impeached Yubian on six counts of factional wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Works section chief Lu Chengyuan then impeached Yubian on six counts of factional corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝雖謫澄源，於汴卒謝事去。

translations.literal: Although the emperor demoted Chengyuan, Yubian in the end resigned from office and left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted Chengyuan, but Yubian ultimately resigned anyway.

sentences.zh: 及辭朝，以敦大進規。

translations.literal: On taking leave of court he offered earnest admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: On his farewell audience he offered earnest counsel to the throne.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 於汴篤誌正學，操履粹白。

translations.literal: Yubian devoted his will to orthodox learning and his conduct was pure and white.
translations.idiomatic: Yubian was devoted to orthodox learning and lived with spotless integrity.

sentences.zh: 立朝，正色不阿，崇獎名教，有古大臣風。

translations.literal: In court he showed stern countenance and did not curry favor, honored and encouraged the teachings of names and relationships, and had the manner of the great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was stern and unbending, upheld moral teaching, and bore the bearing of the great ministers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 孫居相，字伯輔，沁水人。

translations.literal: Sun Juxiang, style name Bofu, was a native of Qinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Juxiang, whose style was Bofu, came from Qinshui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除恩縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of En county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of En county.

sentences.zh: 征授南京御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and made a censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital and appointed censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 負氣敢言。

translations.literal: He was proud in spirit and dared to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and outspoken, he did not shrink from speaking his mind.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏陳時政，謂：「今內自宰執，外至郡守縣令，無一人得盡其職。

translations.literal: He once memorialized on current policy, saying: "Today, from the chief ministers within to prefects and magistrates without, not one man is able fully to perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized on affairs of state, saying: "From the chief ministers within to prefects and magistrates without, not one man can fully perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 政事日廢，治道日乖，天變人怨，究且瓦解土崩。

translations.literal: Government affairs daily decay, the way of governance daily goes astray, heaven's warnings and men's resentments—in the end it will dissolve and crumble like earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Government grows more feeble by the day, the way of rule more perverse, heaven sends warnings and the people seethe with resentment—and in the end the state will collapse like a mound of earth.

sentences.zh: 縱珠玉金寶亙地彌天，何救危亂！

translations.literal: Even if pearls, jade, gold, and treasure covered the earth and filled the sky, how could they save peril and disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Even if pearls and gold covered the earth from horizon to horizon, what good would they do against such peril!

sentences.zh: 」帝不省。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not reflect on it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉世延屢犯重辟，廢為庶人，錮原籍。

translations.literal: The Earl of Sincerity Liu Shiyan repeatedly committed capital offenses, was degraded to commoner status, and was confined to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Earl of Sincerity Liu Shiyan had repeatedly committed capital crimes, was reduced to commoner status, and was confined to his native district.

sentences.zh: 不奉詔，久居南京，益不法，妄言星變，將勒兵赴闕。

translations.literal: He did not obey the edict, long resided at Nanjing, grew ever more lawless, spoke rashly of celestial omens, and was about to force troops to march to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the edict, lingered in Nanjing, grew more lawless, spread rumors of celestial omens, and plotted to march troops on the capital.

sentences.zh: 居相疏發其奸，並及南京勛臣子弟暴橫狀。

translations.literal: Juxiang memorialized to expose his crimes, and also the violent and overbearing conduct of the sons and younger brothers of meritorious ministers at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Juxiang exposed his crimes in a memorial and also denounced the violent conduct of noble heirs at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 得旨下世延吏，安遠、東寧、忻城諸侯伯子弟悉按問，強暴為戢。

translations.literal: An imperial order was obtained to send Shiyan to the judicial authorities; the sons and younger brothers of the marquises and earls of Anyuan, Dongning, Xincheng, and others were all investigated, and violence was quelled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Shiyan to the courts, and the sons of the Anyuan, Dongning, and Xincheng nobles were all investigated until violence subsided.

sentences.zh: 稅使楊榮激變雲南，守太和山中官黃勛嗾道士毆辱知府，居相皆極論其罪。

translations.literal: The tax commissioner Yang Rong provoked rebellion in Yunnan; the eunuch Huang Xun, guarding Mount Taihe, incited Daoist priests to beat and insult the prefect—Juxiang argued their crimes to the utmost in each case.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioner Yang Rong provoked an uprising in Yunnan; eunuch Huang Xun, guarding Mount Taihe, incited Daoist priests to assault the prefect—and Juxiang pressed the full weight of the law against them all.

sentences.zh: 時中外多缺官，居相兼攝七差，署諸道印，事皆辦治。

translations.literal: At the time many offices were vacant inside and outside the capital; Juxiang concurrently held seven posts, affixed the seals of various circuits, and all affairs were handled and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Many posts stood vacant at court and in the provinces. Juxiang held seven concurrent appointments, sealed documents for multiple circuits, and handled every matter competently.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫數被人言，居相力詆其奸貪植黨，一貫乃去，居相亦奪祿一年。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan had repeatedly been spoken against; Juxiang fiercely denounced his treachery, greed, and faction-building—Yiguan then left, and Juxiang also had his salary stripped for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan had long been a target of criticism. Juxiang fiercely denounced his corruption and faction-building. Yiguan resigned, and Juxiang too lost a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 連遭內外艱。

translations.literal: He suffered bereavement within and without in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered successive bereavements at home and in office.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起官，出巡漕運，還發湯賓尹、韓敬科場事。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he took office again, went out to inspect the grain transport, and on return exposed the examination-hall affair of Tang Binyin and Han Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned to office, inspected the grain transport, and on his return exposed the examination scandal involving Tang Binyin and Han Jing.

sentences.zh: 廷議當褫官，其黨為營護，旨下法司覆勘。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that offices should be stripped; their faction worked to protect them, and an edict sent the case to the judicial authorities for re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed they should be stripped of office, but their faction intervened and an edict sent the case back to the judiciary for review.

sentences.zh: 居相復發敬通賄狀，敬遂不振。

translations.literal: Juxiang again exposed Jing's bribery, and Jing then did not recover his standing.
translations.idiomatic: Juxiang exposed Han Jing's bribery anew, and Jing never recovered his standing.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史年例外轉，吏部、都察院協議。

translations.literal: By precedent, when censors were transferred outside the annual rule, the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent transfers of censors outside the regular rotation required joint deliberation by the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 王時熙、魏雲中之去，都御史孫瑋不與聞。

translations.literal: When Wang Shixi and Wei Yunzhong departed, Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei was not consulted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shixi and Wei Yunzhong were transferred out, Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei was not consulted.

sentences.zh: 居相再疏劾尚書趙煥，煥引退。

translations.literal: Juxiang again memorialized to impeach Minister Zhao Huan, and Huan withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Juxiang impeached Minister Zhao Huan again, and Huan resigned.

sentences.zh: 及鄭繼之代煥，復以私意出宋槃、潘之祥於外，居相亦據法力爭。

translations.literal: When Zheng Jizhi replaced Huan, he again sent Song Pan and Pan Zhixiang outside by private intent; Juxiang also resisted by law and strove with force.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jizhi succeeded Huan, he again sent Song Pan and Pan Zhixiang out on personal grounds, and Juxiang fought the decision on legal grounds.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎方從哲由中旨起官，中書張光房等五人以持議不合時貴，擯不與科道選，居相並抗章論列。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Congzhe was raised to office by imperial rescript; the five Secretariat drafters Zhang Guangfang and others, because their views did not accord with the powerful of the time, were excluded from selection in the censorate and supervising secretariats—Juxiang resisted with memorials on all counts.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Fang Congzhe was appointed by imperial rescript. Five secretariat drafters including Zhang Guangfang, whose views offended the powerful, were barred from censorial selection—and Juxiang protested each case in turn.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朋黨勢成，言路不肖者率附吏部，以驅除異己，勢張甚。

translations.literal: At that time factional power had taken shape; unworthy men on the speaking path generally attached themselves to the Ministry of Personnel to drive out those unlike themselves, and their power swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: By then factions were entrenched. Unworthy men in the censorate attached themselves to the Ministry of Personnel to purge opponents, and their power swelled.

sentences.zh: 居相挺身與抗，氣不少沮。

translations.literal: Juxiang stood forth to resist them, his spirit not diminished in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Juxiang stood up to them without flinching.

sentences.zh: 於是過庭訓、唐世濟、李征儀、劉光復、趙興邦、周永春、姚宗文、吳亮嗣、汪有功、王萬祚輩群起為難，居相連疏搘拄，諸人迄不能害。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guo Tingxun, Tang Shiji, Li Zhengyi, Liu Guangfu, Zhao Xingbang, Zhou Yongchun, Yao Zongwen, Wu Liangsi, Wang Yougong, Wang Wanzuo, and their like rose together to make trouble; Juxiang submitted memorial after memorial in support, and in the end they could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tingxun, Tang Shiji, Li Zhengyi, Liu Guangfu, Zhao Xingbang, Zhou Yongchun, Yao Zongwen, Wu Liangsi, Wang Yougong, Wang Wanzuo, and others attacked in concert. Juxiang countered with a stream of memorials, and they could not bring him down.

sentences.zh: 至四十五年，亦以年例出居相江西參政，引疾不就。

translations.literal: By the forty-fifth year Juxiang too was sent out under the annual rule as administrative commissioner of Jiangxi; he cited illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he too was rotated out as Jiangxi administrative commissioner under the regular rule, but he cited illness and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 天啟改元，起光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When the Tianqi reign era was inaugurated he was raised to Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianqi reign began he was recalled as Junior Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 改太仆，擢右僉都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Court of the Imperial Stud, advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and made grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to the Court of the Imperial Stud, then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 四年春，召拜兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 其冬，魏忠賢盜柄，復引疾歸。

translations.literal: That winter Wei Zhongxian usurped power; he again resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as Wei Zhongxian seized power, he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 無何，給事中陳序謂居相出趙南星門，與楊漣交好，序同官虞廷陛又劾居相力薦李三才，遙結史記事，遂削奪。

translations.literal: Before long the supervising secretary Chen Xu said Juxiang had come from Zhao Nanxing's school and was friendly with Yang Lian; Chen's colleague Yu Tingbi also impeached Juxiang for strongly recommending Li Sancai and linking at a distance with Shi Jishi—and he was stripped and penalized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon supervising secretary Chen Xu denounced Juxiang as a follower of Zhao Nanxing and ally of Yang Lian. Chen's colleague Yu Tingbi accused him of promoting Li Sancai and conspiring with Shi Jishi—and Juxiang was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起戶部右侍郎，專督鼓鑄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was raised to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, with exclusive charge of coinage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of coinage.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部，進左侍郎，以戶部尚書總督倉場。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Personnel, advanced to Left Vice Minister, and as Minister of Revenue supervised the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Personnel, promoted to Left Vice Minister, and as Minister of Revenue supervised the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 轉漕多雇民舟，民憊甚，以居相言獲蘇。

translations.literal: Grain transport largely hired civilian boats, and the people were greatly exhausted; through Juxiang's words they obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport relied heavily on hired civilian boats, exhausting the people—but Juxiang's intervention brought them relief.

sentences.zh: 高平知縣喬淳貪虐，為給事中楊時化所劾，坐贓二萬有奇。

translations.literal: The Gaoping magistrate Qiao Chun was greedy and cruel; he was impeached by the supervising secretary Yang Shihua and found guilty of embezzling more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping magistrate Qiao Chun was corrupt and brutal. Supervising secretary Yang Shihua impeached him for embezzling more than twenty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 淳家京師，有奧援，乞移法司覆訊，且訐時化請囑致隙。

translations.literal: Chun's family was in the capital and had hidden backing; he asked that the case be moved to the judicial authorities for re-interrogation, and also accused Shihua of soliciting favors and creating a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's family had powerful connections in the capital. He asked for a retrial in the judiciary and accused Shihua of soliciting favors to create a feud.

sentences.zh: 時化方憂居，通書居相，報書有「國事日非，邪氛益惡」語，為偵事者所得，聞於朝。

translations.literal: Shihua was then in mourning residence; he sent a letter to Juxiang, and the reply contained the words "state affairs daily worsen, evil atmosphere daily grows worse"—it was obtained by spies and heard at court.
translations.idiomatic: Shihua was in mourning and wrote to Juxiang. Juxiang's reply said that "state affairs grow worse by the day and the atmosphere of corruption grows worse." Spies intercepted the letter and it reached the court.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下居相獄，謫戍邊。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, sent Juxiang to prison, and banished him to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, imprisoned Juxiang, and banished him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒於戍所。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He died in exile in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 弟鼎相，歷吏部郎中、副都御史，巡撫湖廣，亦有名東林中。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dingsiang served in succession as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, Deputy Censor-in-Chief, and grand coordinator of Huguang, and was also renowned among the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dingsiang served as bureau director in Personnel, Deputy Censor-in-Chief, and grand coordinator of Huguang, and was likewise noted among the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 曹光，字用韋，益都人。

translations.literal: Cao Guang, style name Yongwei, was a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guang, whose style was Yongwei, came from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，督皇城四門。

translations.literal: He was appointed a section chief in the Ministry of Revenue and supervised the four gates of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a section chief in the Ministry of Revenue with charge of the four gates of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 倉衛軍貸群珰子錢，償以月餉，軍不支餉者三年。

translations.literal: The depot guards borrowed money from the eunuchs' sons, repaying with monthly stipends, and for three years the troops received no pay.
translations.idiomatic: Depot guards borrowed from eunuchs' sons and repaid from monthly stipends, so for three years the troops went unpaid.

sentences.zh: 及餉期，群珰抱券至，光命減息，珰大嘩。

translations.literal: When pay day came the eunuchs arrived clutching their bonds; Guang ordered interest reduced, and the eunuchs raised a great outcry.
translations.idiomatic: When pay day came the eunuchs arrived with their bonds. Guang ordered interest reduced, and they protested loudly.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「並私券奏聞，聽上處分耳。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Submit the private bonds together in a memorial and let the emperor decide.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Submit these private bonds together in a memorial and let the emperor decide.

sentences.zh: 」群珰請如命，軍困稍蘇。

translations.literal: " The eunuchs asked to follow the order, and the troops' distress was somewhat relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuchs complied, and the troops' hardship eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 以憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 起補兵部武選主事，歷職方郎中。

translations.literal: On recall he filled the post of section chief for military selection in the Ministry of War and served in succession as director in the Bureau of Operations.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he served as section chief for military selection in the Ministry of War and rose to director in the Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 大珰私人求大帥，光不可。

translations.literal: A great eunuch's private agent sought a major command; Guang would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: A great eunuch's agent sought a major command for a protégé; Guang refused.

sentences.zh: 東廠太監盧受疏申職掌，光亦請敕受約束部卒，毋陷良民。

translations.literal: The Eastern Depot director Lu Shou memorialized to assert his jurisdiction; Guang also asked that an edict bind Shou to restrain his troops and not entrap innocent people.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Depot director Lu Shou memorialized to assert his jurisdiction. Guang asked that an edict bind Shou to restrain his men and not entrap innocent civilians.

sentences.zh: 稍遷河東參政，引疾歸。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to be administrative commissioner of Hedong and resigned citing illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrative commissioner of Hedong, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，起南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was raised to Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled as Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 光宗驟崩，馳疏言：「先帝春秋鼎盛，奄棄群臣，道路鹹知奸黨陰謀，醫藥雜進，以至於此。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong died suddenly, he rushed a memorial saying: "The late emperor was in the prime of life yet suddenly abandoned his ministers; everyone on the roads knows the wicked faction's secret plot, with medicines mixed and administered, leading to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong died suddenly, Guang rushed a memorial: "The late emperor was in his prime yet suddenly abandoned his ministers. Everyone knows the wicked faction plotted in secret, administering mixed medicines until this end.

sentences.zh: 天下之弒逆，有毒而非鴆、戕而非刃者，此與先年梃擊，同一奸宄。

translations.literal: Among regicides under Heaven there are those poisoned yet not by aconite, killed yet not by blade—this is the same villain as the club attack of years before.
translations.idiomatic: Regicide need not use aconite or a blade. This is the same villainy as the club attack years before.

sentences.zh: 乞明詔輔臣，直窮奸狀，以雪先帝之仇。

translations.literal: I beg a clear edict to the assisting ministers to pursue the villainy to the end and avenge the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that assisting ministers be clearly ordered to pursue the villains to the end and avenge the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " Acknowledgment was received.
translations.idiomatic: " The court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，敘職方時邊功，加光祿卿，進太常大理卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, for frontier merit during his time in the Bureau of Operations, he was given the rank of Minister of Imperial Entertainments and advanced to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianqi, frontier merit from his Bureau of Operations service won him promotion to Minister of Imperial Entertainments and then joint head of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢亂政，大獄紛起，光請告歸。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian threw government into disorder and great cases arose one after another; Guang requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: As Wei Zhongxian threw the government into chaos and political trials multiplied, Guang asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋為給事中潘士聞所劾，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached by the supervising secretary Pan Shiwen, stripped of office, and ordered to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon supervising secretary Pan Shiwen impeached him, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 御史盧承欽歷攻東林，詆光狎主邪盟，遂削奪。

translations.literal: The censor Lu Chengqin repeatedly attacked the Donglin, slandered Guang as intimate master of an evil alliance, and he was stripped and penalized.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Chengqin repeatedly attacked the Donglin, accused Guang of leading a corrupt alliance, and he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起戶部右侍郎，督錢法，尋遷左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was raised to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, supervised the coinage laws, and soon transferred to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of coinage, then promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光初名珍，避仁宗諱，始改名。

translations.literal: Guang's original name was Zhen; to avoid the taboo on the Renzong emperor's name he first changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was originally named Zhen; he changed his name to avoid the taboo on the Renzong emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 五年，陵工成，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the mausoleum works were completed, he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the mausoleum works were completed, he was honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 桂王重建府第，議加江西、河南、山東、山西田賦十二萬有奇；

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui rebuilt his princely residence; it was proposed to add more than one hundred twenty thousand to the land tax of Jiangxi, Henan, Shandong, and Shanxi;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui rebuilt his mansion, and a proposal would add more than 120,000 taels to land taxes in Jiangxi, Henan, Shandong, and Shanxi;

sentences.zh: 浙江逋織造銀十余萬，巡撫陸完學請編入正額。

translations.literal: Zhejiang owed more than one hundred thousand in weaving-office silver; the grand coordinator Lu Wanxue asked that it be incorporated into the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang owed more than 100,000 taels in weaving-office arrears; grand coordinator Lu Wanxue asked to fold them into the regular tax quota.

sentences.zh: 光皆持不可。

translations.literal: Guang held all these inadmissible.
translations.idiomatic: Guang opposed every proposal.

sentences.zh: 中官張彜憲總理戶、工兩部事，議設座於部堂，光不可。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Yixian supervised the affairs of the Ministries of Revenue and Works and proposed setting a seat in the ministry hall; Guang would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Zhang Yixian took charge of Revenue and Works affairs and proposed a seat in the ministry hall; Guang refused.

sentences.zh: 右侍郎高弘圖履任，彜憲欲共設公座，光與弘圖約，比彜憲至，皆曰「事竣矣」，撤座去，彜憲怏怏。

translations.literal: Right Vice Minister Gao Hongtu took up his post; Yixian wished to set up a joint public seat; Guang and Hongtu agreed that when Yixian arrived they would both say "the business is finished," remove the seat, and leave—Yixian was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Minister Gao Hongtu took office. Yixian wanted a joint seat in the hall. Guang and Hongtu agreed that when Yixian arrived they would say the business was done and remove the seat. Yixian was furious.

sentences.zh: 及主事金鉉、馮元飏交疏劾彜憲，彜憲疑出光，日捃摭其隙。

translations.literal: When the section chiefs Jin Xuan and Feng Yuanyang submitted alternating memorials impeaching Yixian, Yixian suspected Guang was behind it and daily gathered material on his faults.
translations.idiomatic: When section chiefs Jin Xuan and Feng Yuanyang impeached Yixian in turn, Yixian suspected Guang and daily hunted for faults.

sentences.zh: 會山永巡撫劉宇烈請料價萬五千兩、鉛五萬斤，工部無給銀例，與鉛之半，宇烈怒，奏鉛皆濫惡。

translations.literal: It happened that the Shanyong grand coordinator Liu Yulie requested material costs of fifteen thousand taels and fifty thousand jin of lead; the Ministry of Works had no precedent for giving silver and gave only half the lead; Yulie was angry and memorialized that all the lead was shoddy and bad.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyong grand coordinator Liu Yulie requested 15,000 taels for materials and 50,000 jin of lead. Works had no precedent for paying silver and supplied only half the lead. Yulie was furious and reported that all the lead was defective.

sentences.zh: 彜憲取粗鉛進曰「庫鉛盡然」，欲以罪光。

translations.literal: Yixian took coarse lead and presented it, saying "all the depot lead is like this," intending to blame Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian presented coarse lead to the throne, claiming all depot stock was the same, intending to blame Guang.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨盡熔庫鉛，司官中毒死者三人，內外官多獲罪。

translations.literal: A stern edict ordered all depot lead melted; three supervising officials died of poisoning, and many officials inside and outside were punished.
translations.idiomatic: A stern edict ordered all depot lead melted. Three officials died from fumes, and many others were punished.

sentences.zh: 彜憲乃糾巡視科道許國榮等十一人，光疏救，忤旨詰責。

translations.literal: Yixian then implicated the touring censorial officials Xu Guorong and eleven others; Guang memorialized to save them and was rebuked by edict for defying the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian then implicated eleven touring censors including Xu Guorong. Guang memorialized in their defense and was rebuked by edict.

sentences.zh: 彜憲又指閘工冒破齮龁之，光累疏乞骸骨歸，五月得請。

translations.literal: Yixian also pointed to embezzlement in the sluice works and gnawed at him; Guang submitted repeated memorials begging to return home on old bones, and in the fifth month obtained permission.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian also accused him over sluice-work embezzlement and harassed him relentlessly. Guang repeatedly asked to retire and was permitted in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 屢薦不起。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly recommended, he did not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly recommended, he never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 家居十四年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home fourteen years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement fourteen years and died.

sentences.zh: 陳於廷，字孟諤，宜興人。

translations.literal: Chen Yuting, style name Meng'e, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuting, whose style was Meng'e, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歷知光山、唐山、秀水三縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Guangshan, Tangshan, and Xiushui counties, was summoned, and made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Guangshan, Tangshan, and Xiushui in turn, then was called to the capital as censor.

sentences.zh: 甫拜命，即論救給事中汪若霖，詆大學士朱賡甚力，坐奪俸一年。

translations.literal: As soon as he received appointment he memorialized to rescue the supervising secretary Wang Ruolin, fiercely denouncing Grand Secretary Zhu Geng, and was penalized by stripping one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office he memorialized to defend supervising secretary Wang Ruolin, fiercely attacking Grand Secretary Zhu Geng, and lost a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 頃之，劾職方郎中申用懋、趙拱極、黃克謙為宰相私人，不宜處要地，又劾賡及王錫爵當斥。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached the Bureau of Operations directors Shen Yongmao, Zhao Gongji, and Huang Keqian as the chief minister's private men, unfit for key posts, and also impeached Geng and Wang Xijue as deserving dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he impeached Bureau of Operations directors Shen Yongmao, Zhao Gongji, and Huang Keqian as the chief minister's creatures, unfit for key posts, and demanded the dismissal of Zhu Geng and Wang Xijue.

sentences.zh: 已，言諭德顧天飐素幹清議，不宜久玷詞林。

translations.literal: Thereafter he said the exposition tutor Gu Tianqi had always led pure criticism and should not long stain the Hanlin grove.
translations.idiomatic: He then argued that exposition tutor Gu Tianqi, a leader of moral criticism, should not long remain in the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 語皆峻切。

translations.literal: His words were all severe and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrances were uniformly sharp and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 視鹺河東，劾稅使張忠撓鹽政。

translations.literal: On inspection of the Hedong salt [monopoly], he impeached tax commissioner Zhang Zhong for obstructing salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the Hedong salt monopoly, he impeached the tax commissioner Zhang Zhong for interfering with salt policy.

sentences.zh: 正陽門災，極陳時政闕失。

translations.literal: When the Zhengyang Gate burned, he set forth at length the failings of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Zhengyang Gate, he presented an extensive memorial detailing failures in government.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服除，起按江西。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed touring censor for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, he was recalled as touring censor for Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時稅務已屬有司，而中官潘相欲親督湖口稅，於廷劾其背旨虐民。

translations.literal: At the time tax affairs already belonged to the civil officials, but eunuch Pan Xiang wished personally to supervise Hukou taxes; Yu Ting impeached him for defying the order and abusing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Tax administration had already been restored to the regular bureaucracy, but the eunuch Pan Xiang sought to supervise Hukou collections in person; Chen Yuting impeached him for violating imperial instructions and oppressing the populace.

sentences.zh: 淮府庶子常洪作奸，論置之法。

translations.literal: Huai princely establishment household officer Chang Hong committed villainy; [Yu Ting] argued he should be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Hong, a household officer of the Huai prince's establishment, committed crimes, he prosecuted him to the full penalty of the law.

sentences.zh: 改按山東。

translations.literal: He was transferred as touring censor to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His post was changed to touring censor in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，擢太仆少卿，徙太常。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, he was promoted vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzong's accession, he was promoted vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and then moved to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 議「紅丸」事，極言崔文升、李可灼當斬。

translations.literal: Debating the "red pill" affair, he strongly declared Cui Wensheng and Li Kezhuo should be decapitated.
translations.idiomatic: In the debate over the "red pill" affair, he argued forcefully that Cui Wensheng and Li Kezhuo deserved execution.

sentences.zh: 尚書王紀被斥，特疏申救。

translations.literal: When Minister Wang Ji was dismissed, he submitted a special memorial to plead for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Rites Wang Ji was dismissed, he filed a special memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 再進大理卿、戶部右侍郎，改吏部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to chief of the Court of Judicial Review, right vice minister of Revenue, transferred to Personnel, and promoted left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again—to chief of the Court of Judicial Review, then right vice minister of Revenue, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and advanced to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙南星既逐，於廷署事。

translations.literal: After Minister Zhao Nanxing was driven out, Yu Ting handled affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Nanxing was ousted as minister, Chen Yuting acted in his capacity.

sentences.zh: 大學士魏廣微傳魏忠賢意，欲用其私人代南星，且許擢於廷總憲，於廷不可，以喬允升、馮從吾、汪應蛟名上。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wei Guangwei conveyed Wei Zhongxian's intent, wishing to use his private man to replace Nanxing, and also promising to promote Yu Ting to censor-in-chief; Yu Ting would not agree and submitted the names of Qiao Yunsheng, Feng Congwu, and Wang Yingjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wei Guangwei relayed Wei Zhongxian's wishes, seeking to install a protégé in Zhao Nanxing's place while offering to promote Chen Yuting to censor-in-chief; Chen Yuting refused and instead nominated Qiao Yunsheng, Feng Congwu, and Wang Yingjiao.

sentences.zh: 忠賢大怒，謂所推仍南星遺黨，矯旨切責，並楊漣、左光鬥盡斥為民。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was greatly enraged, saying those recommended were still Nanxing's remnant faction; he forged an edict sternly rebuking them, and together with Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou all were expelled as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was furious, denouncing the nominees as remnants of Zhao Nanxing's faction; a forged edict sharply rebuked them, and Chen Yuting was expelled to commoner status along with Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou.

sentences.zh: 文選郎張可前、御史袁化中、房可壯亦坐貶黜。

translations.literal: Selection bureau director Zhang Keqian and censors Yuan Huazhong and Fang Kezhuang also were implicated and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Selection bureau director Zhang Keqian and censors Yuan Huazhong and Fang Kezhuang were demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 自是清流盡逐，小人日用事矣。

translations.literal: From this the clear stream [of upright officials] was all driven out, and petty men daily handled affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the upright faction was cleared out, and favor-seekers ran the government day by day.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起南京右都御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, he was recalled as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as right censor-in-chief in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 與鄭三俊典京察，盡去諸不肖者。

translations.literal: Together with Zheng Sanjun he presided over the capital evaluation and completely removed all unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: With Zheng Sanjun he conducted the metropolitan officials' review and purged every unfit appointee.

sentences.zh: 南御史差竣，例聽北考，於廷請先考於南，報可。

translations.literal: When southern censors' assignments finished, by precedent they awaited northern evaluation; Yu Ting requested evaluation first in the south, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing censors completed their tours, precedent called for evaluation in the north; Chen Yuting petitioned for southern evaluation first, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 召拜左都御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 以巡方責重，列上糾大吏、薦人才、修荒政、核屯鹽、禁耗羨、清獄囚、訪奸豪、弭寇盜八事，請於回道日核實課功。

translations.literal: Because touring inspection duties were weighty, he listed eight items—impeach great officials, recommend talent, repair famine administration, check military colonies and salt, forbid surcharges, clear prison inmates, investigate powerful scoundrels, quell banditry—and requested that on the day of return to duty performance be verified and merit assessed.
translations.idiomatic: Given the heavy responsibilities of provincial inspection, he submitted eight proposals: impeach senior officials, recommend talent, repair famine relief, audit garrison colonies and salt, ban illicit surcharges, clear the prisons, investigate powerful wrongdoers, and suppress banditry—asking that performance be verified when censors returned from tour.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒納。

translations.literal: An excellent edict praised and accepted [them].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with an approving edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 給事中馬思理，御史高倬、余文縉坐事下吏，並抗疏救之。

translations.literal: Supervising-secretary Ma Sili and censors Gao Zhuo and Yu Wenjin, implicated in cases, were handed to judicial officers; he jointly submitted vehement memorials to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When supervising-secretary Ma Sili and censors Gao Zhuo and Yu Wenjin were imprisoned on charges, he filed forceful memorials in defense of all three.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三疏乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Three times he memorialized begging retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials requesting retirement, but each was denied.

sentences.zh: 兩浙巡鹽御史祝徽、廣西巡按御史畢佐周並擅撻指揮，非故事。

translations.literal: Zhejiang salt-inspecting censor Zhu Hui and Guangxi touring censor Bi Zuozhou both on their own authority flogged military commanders—not according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui, the Zhejiang salt censor, and Bi Zuozhou, the Guangxi touring censor, had both flogged military commanders on their own authority—contrary to precedent.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝方念疆場多故，欲倚武臣，旨下參核。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor was then mindful that the borders had many troubles and wished to rely on military officers; an order went down to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the reports reached the throne, the emperor—mindful of crises on the frontiers and eager to lean on military commanders—ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 於廷等言：「軍官起世胄，率不循法度，概列彈章，將不勝擾，故小過薄責以懲。

translations.literal: Yu Ting and others said: "Military officers, raised from hereditary houses, mostly do not follow regulations; if impeachment memorials were lodged across the board they could not bear the harassment, so on minor faults light punishment was used as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuting and others argued: "Military officers, drawn from hereditary families, mostly disregard regulations; if censors filed impeachments indiscriminately, commanders would be overwhelmed, so minor offenses have been punished lightly as a warning.

sentences.zh: 凡御史在外者盡然，不自二臣始。

translations.literal: All censors abroad do the same; it did not begin with these two officials."
translations.idiomatic: Every censor on provincial assignment has done the same; this did not begin with these two men alone."

sentences.zh: 」帝以指揮秩崇，非御史得杖，令會兵部稽典制以聞，典制實無杖指揮事，乃引巡撫敕書提問四品武職語以對。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that commanders' rank was exalted and censors had no authority to beat them, ordered a joint review with the Ministry of War against the regulations and report; the regulations in fact had no beating of commanders, so [Yu Ting] cited the language in grand coordinators' commissions on interrogating fourth-rank military posts in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that commanders' rank was too exalted for censors to flog them and ordered the Ministry of War to check the regulations and report back; the regulations in fact contained no provision for beating commanders, so Chen Yuting cited the language in grand coordinators' commissions authorizing interrogation of fourth-rank military officers.

sentences.zh: 帝以比擬不倫，責令再核，於廷等終右御史，所援引悉不當帝意。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed the analogy improper, ordered further investigation; Yu Ting and others ultimately sided with the censors, and all citations failed to satisfy the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed the analogy improper and ordered a further review; Chen Yuting and his colleagues continued to defend the censors, and every precedent they cited failed to satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 疏三上三卻，竟削籍歸。

translations.literal: His memorial was thrice submitted and thrice rejected; in the end his name was struck from the rolls and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials and was rebuffed three times; in the end he was struck from the register and sent home.

sentences.zh: 家居二年卒。

translations.literal: After two years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died two years after returning to private life.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈少保。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously ennobled as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 於廷端亮有守。

translations.literal: Yu Ting was upright, bright, and principled.
