translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuting was upright, principled, and unwavering.

sentences.zh: 周延儒當國，於廷其裏人，無所附麗。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yanru held power, Yu Ting was his townsman but attached himself to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru dominated the government, Chen Yuting was his fellow townsman yet would attach himself to no faction.

sentences.zh: 與溫體仁不合，故卒獲重譴去。

translations.literal: He did not agree with Wen Tiren, and so in the end received severe punishment and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was at odds with Wen Tiren, and in the end incurred severe punishment and left office.

sentences.zh: 鄭三俊，字用章，池州建德人。

translations.literal: Zheng Sanjun, styled Yongzhang, a native of Jiande in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun, styled Yongzhang, was a native of Jiande in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-sixth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授元氏知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京禮部郎中、歸德知府、福建提學副使。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to bureau director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, prefect of Guide, and vice commissioner of education for Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of bureau director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, prefect of Guide, and Fujian vice commissioner of education.

sentences.zh: 家居七年，起故官，督浙江糧儲。

translations.literal: Seven years at home, then recalled to his former office to supervise Zhejiang grain storage.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in retirement he was recalled to his former rank to supervise grain storage in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，召為光祿少卿，改太常。

translations.literal: Early Tianqi, summoned as vice minister of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 未上，陳中官侵冒六事。

translations.literal: Before taking up the post, he memorialized on six matters of eunuch encroachment and embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed office, he memorialized on six abuses of eunuch encroachment and embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 時魏忠賢、客氏離間後妃，希得見帝，而三俊疏有「篤厚三宮，妖冶不列於禦」語。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke sowed discord among the palace women and hoped to see the emperor; Sanjun's memorial had the words "sincere kindness to the three palaces; seductive beauty not listed in the imperial presence."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke were sowing discord among the palace women and angling for access to the emperor; Zheng Sanjun's memorial contained the phrase "show sincere devotion to the three palaces; let no seductive beauty appear before the throne."

sentences.zh: 忠賢遣二豎至閣中，摘「妖冶」語，令重其罪，閣臣力爭，而擬旨則以先朝故事為辭。

translations.literal: Zhongxian sent two palace boys to the Grand Secretariat, plucking out the "seductive beauty" phrase to have the crime weighted heavier; grand secretaries strove in argument, but the draft rescript pleaded precedent from previous reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian sent two palace attendants to the Grand Secretariat to seize on the words "seductive beauty" and demand a heavier penalty; the grand secretaries argued strenuously, but the draft rescript cited precedent from earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 三俊復疏言：「近日麋爛荼毒，無逾中珰，閣臣悉指為故事。

translations.literal: Sanjun again memorialized: "Of late the rot and poison have nothing to exceed the inner eunuchs; grand secretaries all cite it as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun memorialized again: "Of late nothing has rotted and poisoned the state more than the inner eunuchs, yet grand secretaries cite everything as precedent.

sentences.zh: 古人言奄豎聞名，非國之福。

translations.literal: The ancients said that when palace eunuchs become renowned by name, it is no blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that when palace eunuchs become famous by name, it is no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 今聞名者已有人，內連外結，恃閣臣彈壓抑損之，而閣臣輒阿諛自溺其職，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Today there are already those known by name; they link inside and outside, relying on grand secretaries to suppress and diminish [criticism], while grand secretaries flatter and drown in their duties—heart-chilling."
translations.idiomatic: Today such men are already notorious; they conspire inside and out, counting on grand secretaries to suppress criticism, while those secretaries flatter and abandon their duties—it is chilling to behold."

sentences.zh: 」忠賢益怒，以語侵內閣，留中不下。

translations.literal: Zhongxian grew angrier; the language attacked the inner cabinet; the memorial was retained and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian grew still angrier; the language impugned the inner cabinet, and the memorial was held back and never promulgated.

sentences.zh: 擢左僉都御史，疏陳兵食大計，規切內外諸司。

translations.literal: Promoted left vice censor-in-chief; he memorialized on major plans for troops and grain, sternly admonishing inner and outer departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and memorialized on grand strategy for troops and provisions, sternly admonishing departments throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中徐大相言事被謫，抗疏救之。

translations.literal: When Personnel bureau director Xu Daxiang memorialized and was banished, he submitted a defiant memorial to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Daxiang, a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, was banished for a memorial, Zheng Sanjun filed a forceful petition in his defense.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, transferred to left assistant censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he was transferred to left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 戶部右侍郎楊漣劾忠賢，三俊亦上疏極論。

translations.literal: Revenue right vice minister Yang Lian impeached Zhongxian; Sanjun also submitted a memorial arguing to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian, right vice minister of Revenue, impeached Wei Zhongxian, Zheng Sanjun also submitted a memorial denouncing him in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 尋署倉場事。

translations.literal: Soon he handled granary affairs in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of granary affairs in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 太倉無一歲蓄，三俊奏行足儲數事。

translations.literal: Great Granary had not a year's store; Sanjun memorialized implementing several measures for full reserves.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Granary held less than a year's supply; Zheng Sanjun memorialized on several measures to restore full reserves.

sentences.zh: 忠賢盡逐漣等，三俊遂引疾去。

translations.literal: Zhongxian drove out Lian and the rest entirely; Sanjun then pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zhongxian had driven out Yang Lian and his allies, Zheng Sanjun pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 明年，忠賢黨張訥請毀天下書院，劾三俊與鄒元標、馮從吾、孫慎行、余懋衡合汙同流，褫職閑住。

translations.literal: Next year Zhang Na of Zhongxian's faction asked to destroy academies empire-wide, impeaching Sanjun together with Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, Sun Shenxing, and Yu Maoheng as sharing the same foul current; offices stripped, idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Na, a member of Wei Zhongxian's faction, petitioned to destroy private academies throughout the empire and impeached Zheng Sanjun together with Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, Sun Shenxing, and Yu Maoheng as birds of a feather; their offices were stripped and they were ordered to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起南京戶部尚書兼掌吏部事。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 1, recalled as Nanjing Minister of Revenue also handling Personnel affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as minister of revenue at Nanjing, with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 南京諸僚多忠賢遺黨，是年京察，三俊澄汰一空。

translations.literal: Nanjing colleagues were mostly Zhongxian's remnant faction; that year's capital evaluation, Sanjun clarified and purged them all.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Nanjing staff were holdovers from Wei Zhongxian's faction; in that year's metropolitan review Zheng Sanjun purged them all.

sentences.zh: 京師被兵，大臣大獲譴。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered military attack, great ministers received heavy blame.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital came under attack, senior ministers were heavily censured.

sentences.zh: 明年春，三俊以建儲入賀，力言：「皇上憂勞少過，人情郁結未宣。

translations.literal: Next spring Sanjun entered to congratulate on establishing the heir, forcefully saying: "Your Majesty's worry and toil slightly exceed measure; popular feeling is pent up and not expressed.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Zheng Sanjun came to the capital to congratulate the establishment of the heir apparent and urged forcefully: "Your Majesty's anxieties and labors have gone somewhat too far; popular sentiment is pent up and has not been heard.

sentences.zh: 百職庶司，救過不贍，上下睽孤，足為隱慮。

translations.literal: The hundred offices and myriad bureaus patch faults without surplus; above and below estranged and isolated—sufficient for hidden concern.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at every level scramble merely to cover mistakes; court and country are estranged—this is cause for grave concern.

sentences.zh: 願保聖躬以保天下，收人心以收封疆。

translations.literal: I wish to preserve the sacred person to preserve all under Heaven, gather people's hearts to recover the borders."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will guard your health to guard the realm, and win back the people's hearts to win back the frontiers."

sentences.zh: 」帝褒納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the advice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 南糧歲額八十二萬七千有奇，積逋至數百萬，而兵部又增兵不已。

translations.literal: Southern grain annual quota 827,000-odd, accumulated arrears reaching millions, while the Ministry of War kept adding troops without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The southern grain quota was more than 827,000 piculs a year, with arrears mounting into the millions, while the Ministry of War kept adding troops without end.

sentences.zh: 三俊初至，倉庫不足一月餉。

translations.literal: When Sanjun first arrived, warehouses held less than one month's rations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Sanjun first took office, the granaries held less than a month's rations.

sentences.zh: 三俊力祛宿弊，糾有司尤怠玩者數人，屢與兵部爭虛冒，久之，士得宿飽。

translations.literal: Sanjun vigorously removed long-standing abuses, impeached several especially negligent officials, repeatedly disputed false claims with the Ministry of War; after long time, troops obtained full rations.
translations.idiomatic: He worked vigorously to uproot longstanding abuses, impeached several especially negligent officials, and repeatedly challenged inflated troop rolls with the Ministry of War; in time the soldiers were reliably fed.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，稅使四出，蕪湖始設關，歲征稅六七萬，泰昌時已停。

translations.literal: Wanli times tax agents went out in all directions; Wuhu first established a pass, yearly levies sixty or seventy thousand; already stopped in Taichang times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, tax commissioners were dispatched everywhere; a customs post was first established at Wuhu, collecting sixty or seventy thousand taels a year, but the levy had been suspended in the Taichang reign.

sentences.zh: 至是，度支益絀，科臣解學龍請增天下關稅，南京宣課司亦增二萬。

translations.literal: By now revenue was increasingly short; censor Xie Xuelong requested increasing empire-wide pass duties; Nanjing revenue office also increased twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By this time revenue was increasingly strained; censor Xie Xuelong proposed raising transit duties empire-wide, and the Nanjing revenue office added twenty thousand taels as well.

sentences.zh: 三俊以為病民，請減其半，以其半征之蕪湖坐賈，戶部遂派蕪湖三萬，復設關征商。

translations.literal: Sanjun thought it harmed the people, asked to halve it, levy half on Wuhu resident merchants; Revenue Ministry then assigned Wuhu thirty thousand, re-established pass to tax merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun argued that this burdened the people and asked to cut the increase in half, levying half of it on resident merchants in Wuhu; the Ministry of Revenue nevertheless assigned Wuhu thirty thousand taels and re-established the post to tax merchants.

sentences.zh: 三俊請罷征，並於工部分司計舟輸課，不稅貨物，皆不從，遂為永制。

translations.literal: Sanjun asked to abolish the levy and have Works branch office count boat transport dues, not tax goods—all refused, and it became permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to abolish the levy and have the Ministry of Works branch count boat-transport fees without taxing cargo; his proposals were all rejected, and the arrangement became permanent.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖、淮安、杭州三關皆隸南戶部，所遣司官李友蘭、霍化鵬、任俶皆貪，三俊悉劾罷之。

translations.literal: Wuhu, Huai'an, Hangzhou three passes all under Nanjing Revenue; dispatched officials Li Youlan, Huo Huapeng, Ren Ju all greedy—Sanjun impeached and dismissed all.
translations.idiomatic: The customs posts at Wuhu, Huai'an, and Hangzhou all fell under the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; the officials Li Youlan, Huo Huapeng, and Ren Ju whom it dispatched were all corrupt, and Zheng Sanjun impeached and removed every one of them.

sentences.zh: 居七年，就移吏部。

translations.literal: After seven years, moved to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，復當京察，斥罷七十八人，時服其公。

translations.literal: Eighth year first month, again capital evaluation, dismissed seventy-eight—contemporaries admired his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year, when the metropolitan review came due again, he dismissed seventy-eight officials; contemporaries admired his fairness.

sentences.zh: 旋上議官評、杜請屬、慎差委三事，帝皆采納。

translations.literal: Soon memorialized on three matters: official evaluation, blocking patronage requests, careful appointments—all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized on three reforms—merit review of officials, blocking favor-seeking, and careful appointments—and the emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 流寇大擾江北，南都震動，三俊數陳防禦策。

translations.literal: Roaming bandits greatly troubled Jiangbei, southern capital shaken; Sanjun several times set forth defense plans.
translations.idiomatic: As roving bandits ravaged the north bank of the Yangtze and the southern capital was shaken, Zheng Sanjun repeatedly submitted defense plans.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎陳子壯下獄，抗疏救之。

translations.literal: Rites vice minister Chen Zizhuang imprisoned; defiant memorial to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Rites Chen Zizhuang was imprisoned, he filed a forceful memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 考績入都，留為刑部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Performance review entering capital; retained as Minister of Justice, added Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving in the capital for his performance review, he was retained as minister of justice and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝以陰陽愆和，命司禮中官錄囚，流徒以下皆減等。

translations.literal: Emperor because yin and yang were discordant ordered Directorate eunuchs to review prisoners; exiles and below all reduced a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Because heaven and earth were out of harmony, the emperor ordered eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial to review prisoners, and all exiles and lesser offenders had their sentences reduced by one grade.

sentences.zh: 三俊以文武諸臣詿誤久系者眾，請令出外候讞。

translations.literal: Sanjun because many civil and military officials long detained on entanglement errors, asked they be sent outside awaiting trial.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun noted that many civil and military officials had been held for long periods on tangled charges and asked that they be released to await trial outside prison.

sentences.zh: 因論告訐株蔓之弊，乞敕「內外諸臣行惻隱實政。

translations.literal: Discussing abuses of informants and implicating branches, begged edict: "Inside and outside all officials practice compassionate practical governance.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to discuss the abuses of informers and guilt by association, and begged an edict that "officials throughout the government should practice compassionate and effective justice.

sentences.zh: 內而五城訊鞫，非重辟不必參送法司；

translations.literal: Within, the Five Wards' interrogation—unless capital offense need not be referred to judiciary;
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital, the Five Wards should interrogate cases, but unless the crime carries the death penalty, cases need not be referred to the judiciary;

sentences.zh: 外而撫按提追，非真犯不必盡解京師；

translations.literal: Outside, grand coordinators' pursuit—unless true offender need not all be sent to capital;
translations.idiomatic: in the provinces, governors and touring censors should pursue offenders, but unless the culprit is genuinely guilty, not every suspect need be sent to the capital;

sentences.zh: 刑曹決斷，以十日為期。

translations.literal: Criminal bureau decisions within ten days as term."
translations.idiomatic: and the Ministry of Justice should decide cases within ten days."

sentences.zh: 」帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor all followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 代州知州郭正中因天變，請舉寒審之典，帝命考故事。

translations.literal: Daizhou prefect Guo Zhengzhong on celestial anomaly requested cold-season review; emperor ordered examining precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhengzhong, prefect of Daizhou, cited a celestial portent to request a winter review of prisoners; the emperor ordered precedents to be investigated.

sentences.zh: 三俊稽歷朝寶訓，得祖宗冬月錄囚數事，備列上奏，寢不行。

translations.literal: Sanjun searched dynastic sacred instructions, found several ancestral winter prisoner review cases, fully listed and submitted; shelved, not enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun searched the sacred instructions of successive reigns, found several instances in which the founding emperors had reviewed prisoners in winter, listed them fully in a memorial, and submitted it; the proposal was shelved and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 前尚書馮英坐事遣戍，其母年九十有一，三俊乞釋還侍養，不許。

translations.literal: Former minister Feng Ying condemned for affair to frontier service; his mother ninety-one; Sanjun begged release to tend her—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Former Minister Feng Ying had been banished for an offense; his mother was ninety-one; Zheng Sanjun begged that he be released to support her, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 初，戶部尚書侯恂坐屯豆事下獄，帝欲重譴之。

translations.literal: Initially Revenue minister Hou Xiong implicated in garrison beans affair imprisoned; emperor wished severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Revenue Hou Xiong had been imprisoned in connection with the garrison-grain affair, and the emperor wished to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 三俊屢讞上，不稱旨。

translations.literal: Sanjun repeatedly judged upward, not according with intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun repeatedly submitted judicial recommendations that failed to satisfy the emperor.

sentences.zh: 讒者謂恂與三俊皆東林，曲法縱舍。

translations.literal: Slanderers said Xiong and Sanjun both Donglin, bent law to leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers claimed that Hou Xiong and Zheng Sanjun, both associated with the Donglin faction, were bending the law to shield one another.

sentences.zh: 工部錢局有盜穴其垣，命按主者罪，三俊亦擬輕典。

translations.literal: Works coin bureau thieves bored hole in wall; ordered investigate responsible party; Sanjun also proposed light statute.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves had tunneled into the wall of the Ministry of Works mint; the emperor ordered an investigation of those responsible, and Zheng Sanjun again proposed a lenient penalty.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，褫其官下吏。

translations.literal: Emperor greatly enraged, stripped office and sent to judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, stripped him of office, and handed him over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 應天府丞徐石麒適在京，上疏力救，忤旨切責。

translations.literal: Yingtian prefectural vice magistrate Xu Shiqi happened in capital, memorialized forcefully to save—contrary to intent sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiqi, vice magistrate of Yingtian prefecture, happened to be in the capital and memorialized forcefully in his defense; he was sharply rebuked for defying the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝御經筵，講官黃景昉稱三俊至清，又偕黃道周各疏救。

translations.literal: Emperor at classics lecture; lecturer Huang Jingfang praised Sanjun extremely pure; together Huang Daozhou each memorialized rescue.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial lecture session Huang Jingfang, the lecturer, praised Zheng Sanjun as exceptionally incorrupt; Huang Daozhou joined him in submitting rescue memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，切責三俊欺罔。

translations.literal: Emperor did not accept, sharply rebuked Sanjun for deception.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not relent and sharply rebuked Zheng Sanjun for deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 以無贓私，令出獄候訊。

translations.literal: Because no corruption, ordered release from prison awaiting trial.
translations.idiomatic: Finding no evidence of graft, he ordered Zheng Sanjun released from prison to await trial.

sentences.zh: 宣大總督盧象升復救之，大學士孔貞運等復以為言，乃許配贖。

translations.literal: Xuan-Da governor Lu Xiangsheng again saved him; grand secretary Kong Zhenyun and others again spoke; then permitted redemption fine.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangsheng, governor-general of Xuanfu and Datong, interceded again, and Grand Secretary Kong Zhenyun and others spoke up once more; only then was he allowed to redeem his sentence by fine.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，召復故官。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, first month—summoned to restore former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year [of Chongzhen], he was summoned to restore his former office.

sentences.zh: 會吏部尚書李日宣得罪，即命三俊代之。

translations.literal: As it happened Minister of Personnel Li Rixuan offended; immediately ordered Sanjun to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Personnel Li Rixuan fell afoul of the throne, the emperor at once appointed Zheng Sanjun in his place.

sentences.zh: 時值考選，外吏多假繕城、墾荒名，減俸行取，都御史劉宗周疏論之。

translations.literal: At the time evaluation and selection were under way; many local officials borrowed names of wall repair and land reclamation, took reduced-salary direct promotion; censor-in-chief Liu Zongzhou memorialized on it.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation and selection were under way; many local officials cited fictitious merits in wall repair and land reclamation to secure reduced-salary promotions to the capital, and Censor-in-Chief Liu Zongzhou memorialized against the practice.

sentences.zh: 諸人乃夤緣周延儒，囑兵部尚書張國維以知兵薦，帝即欲召對親擢。

translations.literal: Those men then curried favor with Zhou Yanru, asked War Minister Zhang Guowei to recommend them as knowing warfare; the emperor at once wished to summon them for audience and personally promote them.
translations.idiomatic: They then curried favor with Zhou Yanru and had War Minister Zhang Guowei recommend them for military talent; the emperor at once wanted to summon them for interview and personal promotion.

sentences.zh: 三俊言：「考選者部、院事，天子且不得專，況樞部乎？

translations.literal: Sanjun said: "Evaluation and selection are the business of the ministry and the censorate; even the Son of Heaven may not monopolize them—how much more the military ministry?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun said, "Evaluation and selection are the business of the Ministry of Personnel and the censorate; even the Son of Heaven may not monopolize them—how much more the Ministry of War?

sentences.zh: 乞先考定，乃請聖裁。

translations.literal: I beg that the evaluation be completed first, and then the sacred decision be requested.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the evaluation be completed first, and only then that the imperial decision be sought.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，召三俊責之，對不屈。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased, summoned Sanjun and rebuked him; he replied without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased, summoned Zheng Sanjun, and rebuked him; he replied without yielding.

sentences.zh: 宗周復言：「三俊欲俟部、院考後，第其優劣純疵，恭請欽定。

translations.literal: Zongzhou again said: "Sanjun wishes to wait until after the ministry and censorate evaluation, rank their excellence and flaws, and respectfully request imperial determination.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou added, "Zheng Sanjun wishes to wait until the Ministry of Personnel and the censorate have finished their evaluation, rank candidates by merit and defect, and respectfully submit them for imperial determination.

sentences.zh: 若但以奏對取人，安能得真品？

translations.literal: If men are chosen only by memorial audience, how can true caliber be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If men are chosen only by interview at court, how can true caliber be obtained?

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，由是幸進者眾。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow; from this those advanced by favor were many.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not agree; from then on, many were advanced by imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔求賢，三俊舉李邦華、劉宗周自代，且薦黃道周、史可法、馮元飏、陳士奇四人。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict seeking worthies; Sanjun recommended Li Banghua and Liu Zongzhou to replace himself, and also recommended Huang Daozhou, Shi Kefa, Feng Yuanyang, and Chen Shiji—four men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict seeking worthies; Zheng Sanjun recommended Li Banghua and Liu Zongzhou to succeed him, and also recommended Huang Daozhou, Shi Kefa, Feng Yuanyang, and Chen Shiji.

sentences.zh: 姜埰、熊開元言事下獄，及宗周獲嚴譴，三俊皆懇救。

translations.literal: Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan spoke on affairs and were imprisoned; when Zongzhou received severe punishment, Sanjun earnestly pleaded for them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan were imprisoned for their memorials, and when Liu Zongzhou received severe punishment, Zheng Sanjun earnestly interceded for them all.

sentences.zh: 先後奏罷不職司官數人，銓曹悉廩廩。

translations.literal: He successively memorialized to dismiss several incompetent bureau officials; the personnel bureau was all trembling.
translations.idiomatic: He successively memorialized to dismiss several incompetent bureau officials, and the personnel bureau trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 大僚缺官，三俊數引薦，賢士之廢斥者多復用。

translations.literal: When high offices lacked incumbents, Sanjun repeatedly recommended men; many worthies who had been dismissed were restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When high offices lacked incumbents, Zheng Sanjun repeatedly recommended candidates, and many dismissed worthies were restored to office.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書徐石麒獲罪，率同官合疏乞留。

translations.literal: When Minister of Justice Xu Shiqi was punished, [Sanjun] led his colleagues in a joint memorial begging that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Justice Xu Shiqi was punished, Zheng Sanjun led his colleagues in a joint memorial begging that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 三俊為人端嚴清亮，正色立朝。

translations.literal: Sanjun as a man was upright, severe, pure, and bright; he stood at court with proper countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun was upright, severe, pure, and bright in character; he stood at court with proper countenance.

sentences.zh: 惟引吳昌時為屬，頗為世詬病。

translations.literal: Only in recommending Wu Changshi as a subordinate was he much reviled by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Only in recommending Wu Changshi as a subordinate was he much criticized by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 時文選缺郎中，儀制郎中吳昌時欲得之。

translations.literal: At the time the Civil Appointments Bureau lacked a director; Wu Changshi, director in the Bureau of Rites Regulations, wished to obtain the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Civil Appointments Bureau lacked a director; Wu Changshi, a director in the Bureau of Rites Regulations, wished to obtain the post.

sentences.zh: 首輔周延儒力薦於帝，且以囑三俊，他輔臣及言官亦多稱其賢，三俊遂請調補。

translations.literal: Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru strongly recommended him to the emperor and also entrusted Sanjun; other grand secretaries and remonstrance officials also often praised his worth, and Sanjun then requested a transfer to fill the vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru strongly recommended him to the emperor and also pressed Zheng Sanjun; other grand secretaries and remonstrance officials likewise praised Wu Changshi, and Zheng Sanjun then requested a transfer to fill the vacancy.

sentences.zh: 帝特召問，三俊復徇眾意以對。

translations.literal: The emperor specially summoned and questioned him; Sanjun again followed the crowd's intent in his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially summoned and questioned him; Zheng Sanjun again followed the crowd's intent in his reply.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之，明日即命下。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded; the next day the order was issued at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded assent; the next day the order was issued at once.

sentences.zh: 以他部調選郎，前此未有也。

translations.literal: To transfer a selection director from another department—never before had this been done.
translations.idiomatic: Transferring a selection director from another department was unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 帝惡言官不職，欲多汰之，嘗以語三俊，三俊與昌時謀出給事四人、御史六人於外。

translations.literal: The emperor hated remonstrance officials for neglecting duty and wished to eliminate many; he once told Sanjun, and Sanjun with Changshi plotted to send out four supervising secretaries and six censors to provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated remonstrance officials for neglecting duty and wished to eliminate many; he once told Zheng Sanjun, who with Wu Changshi plotted to send out four supervising secretaries and six censors to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史大嘩，謂昌時紊制弄權，連章力攻，並詆三俊。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries and censors raised a great uproar, saying Changshi disordered institutions and manipulated power; they linked memorials and forcefully attacked, and also slandered Sanjun.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries and censors raised a great uproar, charging that Wu Changshi disordered institutions and manipulated power; they submitted linked memorials attacking him forcefully and also slandered Zheng Sanjun.

sentences.zh: 三俊懇乞休致，詔許乘傳歸。

translations.literal: Sanjun earnestly begged to retire; an edict permitted him to return home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Sanjun earnestly begged to retire; an edict permitted him to return home by relay post.

sentences.zh: 國變後，家居十余年乃卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic collapse, he dwelt at home for more than ten years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty, he lived in retirement for more than ten years before he died.

sentences.zh: 李日宣，字晦伯，吉水人。

translations.literal: Li Rixuan, style Huibo, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rixuan, style Huibo, was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed a court document drafter and was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a court document drafter and was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，遼陽破。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 請帝時召大僚，面決庶政。

translations.literal: He asked that the emperor at times summon high ministers to decide common affairs face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the emperor at times summon high ministers to decide routine affairs face to face.

sentences.zh: 尋請宥侯震旸以開言路，厚中宮以肅名分。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to pardon Hou Zhenyang to open the path of speech, and to enrich the inner palace to solemnize name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to pardon Hou Zhenyang to open the path of remonstrance, and to enrich the inner palace to solemnize name and rank.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切責。

translations.literal: He defied the imperial will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: He defied the imperial will and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 已，又薦丁元薦、鄒維璉、麻僖等十余人，乞召還朱欽相、劉廷宣等，帝以濫薦逐臣，停俸三月。

translations.literal: Later he again recommended Ding Yuanjian, Zou Weilian, Ma Xi, and more than ten others, and begged to recall Zhu Qinxiang, Liu Tingxuan, and others; the emperor, on grounds of indiscriminate recommendation of banished ministers, stopped his salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again recommended Ding Yuanjian, Zou Weilian, Ma Xi, and more than ten others, and begged to recall Zhu Qinxiang, Liu Tingxuan, and others; the emperor, charging indiscriminate recommendation of banished ministers, stopped his salary for three months.

sentences.zh: 旋出理河東鹽政。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was sent out to manage Hedong salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was sent out to manage Hedong salt administration.

sentences.zh: 還朝，以族父邦華佐兵部，引嫌歸。

translations.literal: On returning to court, because his clansman Banghua was assisting the Ministry of War, he cited scruple and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, because his clansman Li Banghua was assisting the Ministry of War, he cited scruple and resigned.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，逆黨倪文煥劾邦華、日宣為東林邪黨，遂削籍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the partisan Ni Wenhuan impeached Banghua and Rixuan as an evil Donglin faction; they were then struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the partisan Ni Wenhuan impeached Li Banghua and Li Rixuan as an evil Donglin faction; they were then struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，復故官，以邦華在朝，久不出。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, [Li Rixuan] was restored to his former office; because Banghua was at court, he long did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, Li Rixuan was restored to his former office; because Li Banghua was at court, he long declined to take office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，起故官，巡按河南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was raised to his former office and toured Henan as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was raised to his former office and toured Henan as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 還朝，掌河南道事。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he held affairs of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he held affairs of the Henan remonstrance circuit.

sentences.zh: 中官王坤訐大學士周延儒，日宣率同官言：「內臣監兵，不宜侵輔臣，且插款中疑，邊情多故，坤責亦不可逭。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Kun accused Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru; Rixuan led his colleagues in saying: "Inner servants who supervise troops should not encroach on grand secretaries; moreover, inserting suspicions into treaties—with the border situation unsettled, Kun's blame also cannot be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Kun accused Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru; Li Rixuan led his colleagues in saying, "Inner servants who supervise troops should not encroach on grand secretaries; moreover, inserting suspicions into treaties—with the border situation unsettled, Wang Kun's guilt also cannot be escaped.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " Acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 遷大理丞，屢進太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was repeatedly promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was repeatedly promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，擢兵部右侍郎，鎮守昌平。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year he was promoted to vice minister of war and garrisoned Changping.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year he was promoted to vice minister of war and garrisoned Changping.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左侍郎，協理戎政。

translations.literal: After a long time he was advanced to left vice minister and co-managed military administration.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was advanced to left vice minister and co-managed military administration.

sentences.zh: 尋敘護陵功，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of merit in guarding the imperial tombs, he was given the additional title of minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on account of merit in guarding the imperial tombs, he was given the additional title of minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，擢吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was promoted to minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，會推閣臣，日宣等以蔣德璟、黃景昉、姜曰廣、王錫袞、倪元璐、楊汝成、楊觀光、李紹賢、鄭三俊、劉宗周、吳甡、惠世揚、王道直名上。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, at joint recommendation for grand secretaries, Rixuan and others submitted the names of Jiang Dejing, Huang Jingfang, Jiang Yueguang, Wang Xichong, Ni Yuanlu, Yang Rucheng, Yang Guanguang, Li Shaoxian, Zheng Sanjun, Liu Zongzhou, Wu Shen, Hui Shiyang, and Wang Daozhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, at joint recommendation for grand secretaries, Li Rixuan and others submitted the names of Jiang Dejing, Huang Jingfang, Jiang Yueguang, Wang Xichong, Ni Yuanlu, Yang Rucheng, Yang Guanguang, Li Shaoxian, Zheng Sanjun, Liu Zongzhou, Wu Shen, Hui Shiyang, and Wang Daozhi.

sentences.zh: 帝令再推數人，而副都御史房可壯、工部右侍郎宋玫、大理寺卿張三謨與焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered several more men to be recommended, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Fang Kezhuang, Vice Minister of Works Song Mei, and Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Sanmo were included.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered several more men to be recommended, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Fang Kezhuang, Vice Minister of Works Song Mei, and Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Sanmo were included.

sentences.zh: 大僚不獲推者，為流言入內，且創二十四氣之說，帝深惑之。

translations.literal: High ministers who were not recommended spread rumors into the inner court and even invented a theory of the "twenty-four qi"; the emperor was deeply confused by it.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers who were not recommended spread rumors into the inner court and even invented a theory of the "twenty-four qi"; the emperor was deeply confused by it.

sentences.zh: 逾月，召日宣及與推諸臣入中左門，偕輔臣賜食。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the emperor summoned Rixuan and the recommending ministers into the central left gate and, together with the grand secretaries, granted them food.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, the emperor summoned Li Rixuan and the recommending ministers into the central left gate and, together with the grand secretaries, granted them food.

sentences.zh: 已，出禦中極殿，令諸臣奏對。

translations.literal: Then he went out to receive them at the Hall of the Central Ultimate and ordered the ministers to speak at audience.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went out to receive them at the Hall of the Central Ultimate and ordered the ministers to speak at audience.

sentences.zh: 玫陳九邊形勢甚辯，帝惡其幹進，叱之，乃命德璟、景昉、甡入閣，而以徇情濫舉責日宣等回奏。

translations.literal: Mei stated the situation on the nine borderlands very eloquently; the emperor hated his pushing for advancement and shouted him down; he then ordered Dejing, Jingfang, and Shen into the cabinet, and charged Rixuan and others to reply on grounds of favoritism and indiscriminate recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Song Mei stated the situation on the nine borderlands very eloquently; the emperor hated his pushing for advancement and shouted him down; he then ordered Jiang Dejing, Huang Jingfang, and Wu Shen into the cabinet, and charged Li Rixuan and the others to reply on grounds of favoritism and indiscriminate recommendation.

sentences.zh: 奏上，帝怒不解，復禦中左門，太子及定、永二王侍。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor's anger did not abate; he again received them at the central left gate, with the crown prince and the princes of Ding and Yong in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor's anger did not abate; he again received them at the central left gate, with the crown prince and the princes of Ding and Yong in attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝召日宣，聲甚厲。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Rixuan; his voice was very harsh.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Li Rixuan; his voice was very harsh.

sentences.zh: 次召吏科都給事中章正宸、河南道御史張煊，及玫、可壯、三謨，詰其妄舉。

translations.literal: Next he summoned Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Circuit Zhang Zhenchen, Henan Circuit Censor Zhang Huang, and Mei, Kezhuang, and Sanmo, and interrogated them on their reckless recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Next he summoned Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Circuit Zhang Zhenchen, Henan Circuit Censor Zhang Huang, and Song Mei, Fang Kezhuang, and Zhang Sanmo, and interrogated them on their reckless recommendation.

sentences.zh: 日宣奏辯。

translations.literal: Rixuan memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rixuan memorialized in defense.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝嘗言秉公執法，今何事不私？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You once said you would uphold the law impartially—now what matter is not private?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You once said you would uphold the law impartially—now what matter is not private?"

sentences.zh: 」正宸奏：「日宣多遊移，臣等常劾之。

translations.literal: " Zhenchen memorialized: "Rixuan is much evasive; we have often impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Zhenchen memorialized, "Li Rixuan is much evasive; we have often impeached him.

sentences.zh: 然推舉事，實無所徇。

translations.literal: Yet on the matter of recommendation, there was truly no favoritism."
translations.idiomatic: Yet on the matter of recommendation, there was truly no favoritism."

sentences.zh: 」日宣復為玫等三人解。

translations.literal: " Rixuan again spoke in defense of Mei and the other three men.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Rixuan again spoke in defense of Song Mei and the other three men.

sentences.zh: 帝命錦衣官提下日宣等六人，並褫冠帶就執。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered brocade-clad guard officers to take down Rixuan and the other six men, stripped their caps and belts, and had them arrested on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered brocade-clad guard officers to take down Li Rixuan and the other six men, stripped their caps and belts, and had them arrested on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時帝怒甚，侍臣皆股栗失色。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor's anger was extreme; the attending ministers all trembled in their thighs and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor's anger was extreme; the attending ministers all trembled and turned pale.

sentences.zh: 德璟、景昉、甡叩頭辭新命，因言：「臣等並在會推中。

translations.literal: Dejing, Jingfang, and Shen kowtowed and declined the new appointment, saying: "We too were all in the joint recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dejing, Huang Jingfang, and Wu Shen kowtowed and declined the new appointment, saying, "We too were all in the joint recommendation.

sentences.zh: 若諸臣有罪，臣等豈能安。

translations.literal: If the various ministers are guilty, how can we be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: If the various ministers are guilty, how can we be at ease?"

sentences.zh: 」大學士周延儒等亦乞優容。

translations.literal: " Grand Secretaries Zhou Yanru and others also begged lenient treatment.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Secretaries Zhou Yanru and others also begged lenient treatment.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不許，遂下刑部。

translations.literal: The emperor would not permit any of it and sent them down to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not permit any of it and sent them down to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 廷臣交章申救，不納，帝疑其未就獄，責刑部臣克期三日定讞。

translations.literal: Court ministers submitted linked memorials pleading for them, but the emperor did not accept; suspecting they had not yet entered prison, he ordered the Ministry of Justice to fix a verdict within three days.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers submitted linked memorials pleading for them, but the emperor did not accept; suspecting they had not yet entered prison, he ordered the Ministry of Justice to fix a verdict within three days.

sentences.zh: 侍郎惠世揚、徐石麒擬予輕比，帝大怒，革世揚職，鐫石麒二秩，郎中以下罪有差。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Hui Shiyang and Xu Shiqi drafted a light sentence; the emperor was greatly enraged, dismissed Shiyang from office, cut Shiqi two ranks, and punished directors and below according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Hui Shiyang and Xu Shiqi drafted a light sentence; the emperor was greatly enraged, dismissed Hui Shiyang from office, cut Xu Shiqi two ranks, and punished directors and below according to degree.

sentences.zh: 御史王漢言：「枚卜一案，日宣等無私。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Han said: "In the cabinet-selection case, Rixuan and the others were without private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Han said, "In the cabinet-selection case, Li Rixuan and the others were without private interest.

sentences.zh: 陛下懷疑，重其罪，刑官莫知所執。

translations.literal: Your Majesty harbors suspicion and has made their guilt heavy; the punishment officials know not what standard to uphold."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty harbors suspicion and has made their guilt heavy; the punishment officials know not what standard to uphold."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He was not listened to.
translations.idiomatic: " He was not listened to.

sentences.zh: 獄上，日宣、正宸、煊戍邊，玫、可壯、三謨削籍。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, Rixuan, Zhenchen, and Huang were exiled to the border; Mei, Kezhuang, and Sanmo were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was submitted, Li Rixuan, Zhang Zhenchen, and Zhang Huang were exiled to the border; Song Mei, Fang Kezhuang, and Zhang Sanmo were struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 久之，赦還，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he was amnestied and returned; he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was amnestied and returned; he died.

sentences.zh: 張瑋，字席之，武進人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, style Xizhi, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, style Xizhi, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，取糠秕自給，不輕受人一飯，為同里薛敷教所知。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he fed himself on chaff and bran and would not lightly accept a single meal from others; he was noticed by his fellow townsman Xue Fujiao.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he fed himself on chaff and bran and would not lightly accept a single meal from others; he was noticed by his fellow townsman Xue Fujiao.

sentences.zh: 講學東林書院，師孫慎行。

translations.literal: He lectured at the Donglin Academy and studied under Sun Shenxing.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured at the Donglin Academy and studied under Sun Shenxing.

sentences.zh: 其學以慎獨研幾為宗。

translations.literal: His learning took cautious solitude and probing of subtle beginnings as its root.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took cautious solitude and probing of subtle beginnings as its root.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十年，舉應天鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Wanli he placed first in the Yingtian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of Wanli he placed first in the Yingtian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 越七年，成進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Seven years later he passed the metropolitan examination, was made a graduate, and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later he passed the metropolitan examination, was made a graduate, and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 調兵部職方，歷郎中，出為廣東提學僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War Bureau of Appointments, served as a director, and went out as education intendant of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of War Bureau of Appointments, served as a director, and went out as education intendant of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 粵俗奢麗，督學至，宮室供張輿馬餼牽之奉甲他省，象犀文石，名花珠具，磊砢璀璨，瑋悉屏去弗視也。

translations.literal: Cantonese customs were luxurious; when the education superintendent arrived, the furnishings of palaces, carriages, horses, and feast gifts exceeded every other province—ivory, rhinoceros horn, carved stone, famous flowers, pearl implements, piled dazzling and bright—and Wei screened them all away and would not look.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese customs were luxurious; when the education superintendent arrived, the furnishings of palaces, carriages, horses, and feast gifts exceeded every other province—ivory, rhinoceros horn, carved stone, famous flowers, pearl implements, piled dazzling and bright—and Zhang Wei screened them all away and would not look.

sentences.zh: 大吏建魏忠賢祠，乞上梁文於瑋，瑋即日引去。

translations.literal: High officials built a temple to Wei Zhongxian and begged a beam-raising essay from Wei; Wei withdrew the same day.
translations.idiomatic: High officials built a temple to Wei Zhongxian and begged a beam-raising essay from Zhang Wei; Zhang Wei withdrew the same day.

sentences.zh: 瑋廉，歸而布袍草履，授徒於家。

translations.literal: Wei was incorruptible; on returning he wore cloth robe and straw sandals and taught disciples at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei was incorruptible; on returning he wore a cloth robe and straw sandals and taught disciples at home.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，起江西參議，歷福建、山東副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, [Wei] was raised to administration commissioner of Jiangxi and served successively as vice commissioner in Fujian and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, Zhang Wei was raised to administration commissioner of Jiangxi and served successively as vice commissioner in Fujian and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 大學士吳宗達謂瑋難進而易退，言之吏部，召為尚寶卿，進太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wu Zongda said Wei was hard to advance and easy to withdraw; he spoke to the Ministry of Personnel, and [Wei] was summoned as director of the Court of Imperial Seals and advanced to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wu Zongda said Zhang Wei was hard to advance and easy to withdraw; he spoke to the Ministry of Personnel, and Zhang Wei was summoned as director of the Court of Imperial Seals and advanced to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 坐事調南京大理丞，引疾去。

translations.literal: On account of an offense he was transferred to vice director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and cited illness in resigning.
translations.idiomatic: On account of an offense he was transferred to vice director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and cited illness in resigning.

sentences.zh: 久之，起應天府丞。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised to vice magistrate of Yingtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was raised to vice magistrate of Yingtian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，四方大旱，瑋以軍食可虞，奏請：「禁江西、湖廣遏糴，而令應天、常、鎮、淮、揚五郡折輸漕糧銀，赴彼易米，則小民免催科之苦，太倉無顆粒之虧。

translations.literal: That year there was great drought in all directions; Wei, because army provisions were to be feared, memorialized requesting: "Forbid grain hoarding in Jiangxi and Huguang, and order the five prefectures of Yingtian, Chang, Zhen, Huai, and Yang to convert their tribute-grain delivery into silver, send it there to exchange for rice—then the common people will be spared the suffering of forced collection, and the great granary will suffer no loss of grain.
translations.idiomatic: That year there was great drought in all directions; Zhang Wei, fearing for army provisions, memorialized requesting, "Forbid grain hoarding in Jiangxi and Huguang, and order the five prefectures of Yingtian, Chang, Zhen, Huai, and Yang to convert their tribute-grain delivery into silver, send it there to exchange for rice—then the common people will be spared the suffering of forced collection, and the great granary will suffer no loss of grain.

sentences.zh: 他十庫所收銅、錫、顏料、皮布，非州縣土產者，悉解折色，且盡改民解為官解，以救民湯火。

translations.literal: As for copper, tin, pigments, hides, and cloth collected in the other ten treasuries that are not products of the counties, let all be remitted in commuted cash; moreover, entirely change people's delivery into official delivery, to rescue the people from boiling fire."
translations.idiomatic: As for copper, tin, pigments, hides, and cloth collected in the other ten treasuries that are not products of the counties, let all be remitted in commuted cash; moreover, entirely change people's delivery into official delivery, to rescue the people from boiling fire."

sentences.zh: 」所司多議行。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices mostly discussed carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible offices mostly discussed carrying it out.

sentences.zh: 遷南京光祿卿，召入為右僉都御史，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Entertainments, summoned in as right vice censor-in-chief, and transferred to left deputy censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Entertainments, summoned in as right vice censor-in-chief, and transferred to left deputy censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時劉宗周、金光辰並總憲紀，瑋乃上《風勵臺班疏》曰：「懲往正以監來。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zongzhou and Jin Guangchen were both overseeing censorate discipline; Wei then submitted a "Memorial to Encourage the Censorate Ranks," saying: "Punish the past to rectify and monitor the future.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Zongzhou and Jin Guangchen were both overseeing censorate discipline; Zhang Wei then submitted a "Memorial to Encourage the Censorate Ranks," saying, "Punish the past to rectify and monitor the future.

sentences.zh: 今極貪則原任巡按蘇松御史王誌舉，極廉則原任南京試御史成勇。

translations.literal: Today the most greedy is former touring inspector of Su-Song, Censor Wang Zhiju; the most incorrupt is former Nanjing trial censor Cheng Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Today the most greedy is former touring inspector of Su-Song, Censor Wang Zhiju; the most incorrupt is former Nanjing trial censor Cheng Yong.

sentences.zh: 勇與臣曾不相知，家居聞勇被逮，士民泣送者萬輩，百里不休。

translations.literal: Yong and I were once strangers; at home I heard Yong was arrested—gentry and commoners who wept and saw him off numbered tens of thousands, for a hundred li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yong and I were once strangers; at home I heard Cheng Yong was arrested—gentry and commoners who wept and saw him off numbered tens of thousands, for a hundred li without cease.

sentences.zh: 後入南都，始知勇在臺不濫聽一辭，不輕贖一鍰，不受屬吏一蔬一果；

translations.literal: Later, on entering the southern capital, I then learned that at the censorate Yong did not indiscriminately hear a single case, did not lightly redeem a single fine, and did not accept from subordinate officials a single vegetable or fruit;
translations.idiomatic: Later, on entering the southern capital, I then learned that at the censorate Cheng Yong did not indiscriminately hear a single case, did not lightly redeem a single fine, and did not accept from subordinate officials a single vegetable or fruit;

sentences.zh: 傑紳悍吏為民害者，不少假借；

translations.literal: toward outstanding gentry and fierce officials who harmed the people, he gave little indulgence;
translations.idiomatic: toward outstanding gentry and fierce officials who harmed the people, he gave little indulgence;

sentences.zh: 委曲開導民以孝弟。

translations.literal: he tactfully guided the people in filial piety and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: he tactfully guided the people in filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 臣離南中，輒扳轅願借成御史，惠我南人。

translations.literal: When I left the south central region, people always pulled at my carriage shaft and wished to borrow Censor Cheng to benefit us southerners.
translations.idiomatic: When I left the south central region, people always pulled at my carriage shaft and wished to borrow Censor Cheng to benefit us southerners.

sentences.zh: 雖前奉嚴譴，宜召為諸御史勸。

translations.literal: Although he before received severe punishment, he ought to be summoned as an encouragement to the censors.
translations.idiomatic: Although he had before received severe punishment, he ought to be summoned as an encouragement to the censors.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，一時稱快。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, all rejoiced at once.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial went up, the court rejoiced as one.

sentences.zh: 詔下誌舉法司逮治，成勇敘用。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: Zhi Ju was sent to the judicial authorities for arrest and punishment, and Cheng Yong was appointed by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Zhi Ju to the courts for punishment and restored Cheng Yong to office.

sentences.zh: 瑋旋以病謝歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Wei soon resigned citing illness and returned home, and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei soon resigned on grounds of illness and went home; he died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈左都御史，謚清惠。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously given Left Censor-in-Chief and the posthumous name Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously honored as Left Censor-in-Chief with the posthumous name Qinghui (Pure Kindness).

sentences.zh: 金光辰，字居垣，全椒人。

translations.literal: Jin Guangchen, style name Juyuan, was a native of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guangchen, whose style was Juyuan, came from Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the first year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a court envoy.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，巡視西城。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and inspected the Western City.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor with charge of inspecting the Western City.

sentences.zh: 內使周二殺人，牒司禮監捕之，其人方直御前，叩頭乞哀。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Zhou Er killed a man; a warrant was sent to the Directorate of Ceremonial to arrest him, but the man was then standing before the emperor and kowtowed begging for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendant Zhou Er committed murder. A warrant went to the Directorate of Ceremonial for his arrest, but he was standing before the emperor and kowtowed for mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此國家法，朕不得私。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is the law of the state; I may not show favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is the law of the state. I cannot show favoritism.

sentences.zh: 」卒抵罪。

translations.literal: " In the end he was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he was punished as the law required.

sentences.zh: 出按河南，條奏至三百余章，彈劾不避權勢。

translations.literal: He went out to tour Henan; his itemized memorials reached more than three hundred chapters, and in impeachment he did not avoid powerful figures.
translations.idiomatic: On tour in Henan he submitted more than three hundred memorials and impeached the powerful without fear.

sentences.zh: 九年，還朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，光辰分守東直門，劾兵部尚書張鳳翼三不可解，一大可憂。

translations.literal: The capital was under martial law; Guangchen shared guard duty at the East Straight Gate and impeached Minister of War Zhang Fengyi for three things impossible to explain and one great cause for alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was placed under martial law, Guangchen helped guard the East Straight Gate and impeached Minister Zhang Fengyi for three inexplicable failures and one grave danger.

sentences.zh: 帝以鳳翼方在行間，寢其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Fengyi was then in the field, shelved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fengyi was in the field, the emperor shelved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 時帝久罷內遣，然以邊警，諸臣類萎腇不任，仍分遣中官盧維寧等總監通、津、臨、德等處兵馬糧餉，而意頗諱言之。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had long ceased inner eunuch missions, yet because of frontier alarms the ministers were mostly timid and incompetent; he still dispatched eunuchs such as Lu Weining to supervise troops, horses, and grain pay at Tong, Jin, Lin, De, and other places, while being rather reluctant to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long stopped sending eunuchs on missions, but with frontier alarms mounting and ministers mostly timid and useless, he again dispatched eunuchs such as Lu Weining to supervise troops and supplies at Tong, Jin, Lin, and De—though he was reluctant to speak openly of it.

sentences.zh: 光辰疏請罷遣，帝怒，召對平臺。

translations.literal: Guangchen memorialized asking that the dispatch be ended; the emperor was angry and summoned him for audience at the Terrace of Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen memorialized to end the eunuch missions. The emperor was furious and summoned him to audience at the Terrace of Peace.

sentences.zh: 風雨驟至，侍臣立雨中，至以袖障溜。

translations.literal: Wind and rain came suddenly; the attending ministers stood in the rain, even using their sleeves to block the runoff.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden storm broke. Attending ministers stood in the rain, some shielding themselves with their sleeves.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝召光辰責之。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor summoned Guangchen and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long wait the emperor summoned Guangchen and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 光辰對曰：「皇上以文武諸臣無實心任事，委任內臣。

translations.literal: Guangchen replied: "Your Majesty, because civil and military ministers lack sincere hearts in performing their duties, entrusts affairs to inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen replied: "Your Majesty entrusts affairs to eunuchs because civil and military officials lack sincere commitment to their duties.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以任內臣，諸臣益弛卸不任。

translations.literal: This foolish subject holds that by entrusting inner eunuchs, the ministers grow all the more slack and incompetent.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that entrusting eunuchs only makes officials more slack and irresponsible.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，聲色俱厲，將重譴光辰，而迅雷直震禦座，風雨聲大作。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angered, voice and countenance both severe, and was about to punish Guangchen heavily, when sudden thunder shook the imperial seat directly and the sound of wind and rain rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage and was about to punish Guangchen severely when thunder shook the throne and the storm broke in full force.

sentences.zh: 光辰因言：「臣往在河南，見皇上撤內臣而喜。

translations.literal: Guangchen then said: "When your servant was formerly in Henan, he saw that when Your Majesty withdrew inner eunuchs the people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen added: "When I was in Henan I saw how glad the people were whenever Your Majesty withdrew the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 」語未終，帝沈吟，即雲「汝言毋復爾」，然意亦稍解。

translations.literal: " Before he finished speaking the emperor pondered, then said, "Do not speak thus again," yet his mind also softened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could finish, the emperor fell silent, then said, "Do not speak that way again"—but his anger had already begun to ease.

sentences.zh: 人謂光辰有天幸雲。

translations.literal: People said Guangchen had Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: People said Heaven had favored Guangchen.

sentences.zh: 時張元佐以兵部右侍郎出守昌平，同時內臣提督天壽山者即日往。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yuanzuo went out as Right Vice Minister of War to guard Changping, while the eunuch supervising Tianshou Mountain departed the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanzuo had just gone out as Right Vice Minister of War to guard Changping, while the eunuch supervising Tianshou Mountain set out the same day.

sentences.zh: 帝顧閣臣曰：「內臣即日往，侍臣三日未出，朕之用內臣過耶？

translations.literal: The emperor turned to the grand secretaries and said: "The eunuch departs today, while the attending minister has not left in three days—have I used inner eunuchs excessively?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to the grand secretaries and said: "The eunuch leaves today, but the minister has not set out in three days—am I relying too heavily on eunuchs?

sentences.zh: 」翼日有詔，光辰鐫三級調外。

translations.literal: " The next day an edict was issued: Guangchen was reduced three ranks and transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day an edict demoted Guangchen three ranks and transferred him to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 久之，由浙江按察司照磨召為大理寺正，進太仆丞。

translations.literal: After a long while, from registrar in the Zhejiang surveillance commission he was summoned to be director of the Court of Judicial Review and advanced to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled from a registrar post in the Zhejiang surveillance commission to be director of the Court of Judicial Review, then promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，復偕諸大臣召對平臺，咨以禦邊、救荒、安民之策。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year he again joined the great ministers in audience at the Terrace of Peace, and was consulted on policies for defending the frontier, relieving famine, and settling the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year he again joined senior ministers in audience at the Terrace of Peace, where the emperor asked for policies on frontier defense, famine relief, and pacifying the people.

sentences.zh: 光辰班最後，時已夜，光辰獨對燭影中，娓娓數百言，帝為聳然聽。

translations.literal: Guangchen ranked last; it was already night; Guangchen alone faced the candlelight and spoke smoothly for several hundred words, and the emperor listened with startled attention.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen spoke last, deep into the night, alone in the candlelight. He spoke at length—several hundred words—and the emperor listened with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 明日諭諸臣各繕疏以進。

translations.literal: The next day the ministers were instructed each to draft a memorial and submit it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor ordered each minister to submit a written memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋移尚寶丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Court of Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 陳罷練總、換授、私派、僉報數事，報聞。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish several matters—the training general, exchange appointments, private assignments, and collective reporting—and acknowledgment was received.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish the training general system, exchange appointments, private assignments, and collective reporting practices. The court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿少卿、左通政。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Junior Minister of Imperial Entertainments and Left Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Junior Minister of Imperial Entertainments and Left Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，復偕諸臣召對德政殿，備陳賊形勢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year he again joined the ministers in audience at the Hall of Virtuous Government and fully set forth the bandits' situation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year he again joined ministers in audience at the Hall of Virtuous Government and gave a full account of the rebel situation.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 無何，以救劉宗周，仍鐫三級調外，事具《宗周傳》。

translations.literal: Before long, for interceding for Liu Zongzhou, he was again reduced three ranks and transferred outside; the affair is fully recorded in the Biography of Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for interceding for Liu Zongzhou, he was again demoted three ranks and sent outside—the full account is in Liu Zongzhou's biography.

sentences.zh: 明年丁父憂。

translations.literal: The next year he suffered his father's bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his father died and he entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起故官。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 未赴，國變，家居二十余年卒。

translations.literal: He did not go; the dynasty changed; he lived at home more than twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the post. The dynasty fell. He lived at home more than twenty years and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明自神宗而後，士大夫峻門戶而重意氣。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: From Emperor Shenzong onward in the Ming, scholar-officials made factional gates steep and valued spirited defiance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: From the Shenzong emperor onward, Ming scholar-officials hardened factional boundaries and prized defiant zeal.

sentences.zh: 其賢者敦厲名檢，居官有所執爭，即清議翕然歸之。

translations.literal: The worthy among them sternly cultivated name and restraint; in office when they had something to uphold and dispute, pure criticism swiftly rallied to them.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy among them cultivated moral discipline; when they took a stand in office, pure criticism rallied to them at once.

sentences.zh: 雖其材識不遠，耳目所熟習，不能不囿於風會，抑亦一時之良也。

translations.literal: Although their talent and insight did not reach far, and what their eyes and ears were accustomed to could not but confine them within the temper of the times, they were nonetheless the good men of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Their talent and vision were limited, and they could not escape the spirit of their age—but they were nonetheless the best men of their time.

sentences.zh: 遭時孔棘，至救過不暇，顧安得責以挽回幹濟之業哉？

translations.literal: They encountered a time of extreme peril, so pressed merely to remedy faults that they had no leisure—how could one demand of them the enterprise of turning back the tide and achieving practical salvation?
translations.idiomatic: They lived in desperate times, struggling merely to stave off disaster—how could one demand of them the grand work of national salvation?
